Now for the long story.
I first saw a quick playtest of Metal Reaper on Steparu's channel, a guy who mostly reviews asian games for PC and smartphone. I was glad to hear N2games exported it overseas. I spent the last few hours levelling some characters and testing out the main features of the game.
The game is unintentionally hilarious, and I like it so.
-Graphics are horrendous to the point where even a well-made modern smart phone game would easily topple Metal Reaper in terms of aesthetics. The launcher would advertise all the classic sexy bunny and maid costumes worn by... Half disfigured women whose faces were comprised of a grand total of 5 polygons.
A better lightning may have helped hide some of the ugliest textures, but since more than half of the stages takes place in daylight, you will have the uncanny chance to enjoy the vast and colorful wastelands of the Nix Empire at full view!
-English is... Oh.
Having korean origins myself, I know for a fact they absolutely hate using google translate or the likes, leading to have million wons-costing huge neon signs mispelled in ways that would make you lose sight, not because it was too bright, but because you have yourself decided to gouge your eyes out, an almost natural reflex man would have when, for example, one is facing an ancient god of the depths in its wake.
Then again, you will most likely not bother reading the quests because of how generic they are. And it's far from being broken to the point where you can't understand♥♥♥♥♥♥ Though I do find it quite amusing when a gigantic camel-riding mad man called "Raider Sniper Leader" attempts to stab with his... Halberd.
If you are to ever play on a korean CS:GO servers, beware of polearm users. They are really the worst.
-In terms of features, Metal Reaper hardly differs from all the good (and terrible) asian MMORPGs. It's mostly about grinding quests and mobs, occasionally venturing is small♥♥♥♥♥dungeons to defeat a big boss with the reaction time of a millenia-old snail on prozac.
There are a few "PVP" events I didn't have the occasion to formally test out, but some of them are really simple in concept, such as the zombie mod, not the CoD one but the CS one. Quite less entertaining due to engine limitations.
The best (read: not bad) part is probably mob bashing. You'll be doing this a lot because, as mentionned, the game gets grindy reel-fo'in-fast. You get to choose between 4 "branches", such as the classic pistol/sniper marksman, the chainsaw-flamethrower wryyyy combo, the machinegun/bazooka hulkogan or the quaint pump shotgun and medpack support. Guess which one I tested out first. Blasting hordes of scorpions and tribals away with a shotty reminded me of my fond times in the West coast of the wastelands trying to get past the enclave troopers to quick-loot Navarro. The controls being quite smooth and with the ability to roll all game long (no stamina bar per se.), you'll find yourself enthralled into this fast paced monster-exploding game.
I did mention everything seems to fly the ♥♥♥♥ away once you finish riddling them with boolets. This would more than make sense if you are using the rocket launcher or a similar heavy duty weapon, but shooting my tiny 9mm at a fat mutated zombie and seeing him ragdoll through the world with greater haste convinced me that this might as well be the best game I have played for years.
Overall, nothing remarkable about this game I'd say. It's a simple, fast paced "hack-and-slash" MMORPG most of you may easily grasp the concept of. If you can get past the terrible engrish and the even more horrendous textures and models, you may find this game to be a lot of fun, for... Oh wait! It's free! What are you waiting for?
I know I did, albeit most likely not in the ways the devs intended us to.

I want to like this game more than I do. And, if you can get it on sale, it might be worth it. It has a good atmosphere, the voice acting is great, and the idea of the game is fantastic.
However, the gameplay is derivative and not particularly great: it uses a cover system for fighting (poorly, in my opinion, since getting into cover doesn't always work well, and you have optic camo, so cover is pointless), the puzzles are interesting but nothing more than "use item A on location B after activating flag C", and much of the time puzzle solving is spent trying to figure out which puzzle you're allowed to solve now.
The story, often said to be it's strongest point, is interesting, but not particularly original or groudbreaking. It's a better (completely linear) story than most video games, but so are most books, movies, and television shows, and a great number can be gotten at a much better value than The Fall. It does have some very clever moments, but it ends with the traditional twist, shock!, instant ending, cliffhanger, "to be continued..." that plague so many other "story-driven" video games, whether indie or AAA.
Was it worth it? I got it on sale, so I'm not particularly upset. Will I buy the sequel? Probably, but mostly because I saw real potential in the developer; this game, on it's own, isn't really worth it to me. But, I do believe, if he can make a really good story (not a good setting or good characters, but a good story), it would be worth my time. The Fall, though? Go play The Swapper instead; it does almost everything this one does, but much, much better.
This game is right up there with Limbo, with a great story, an intriguing ambience, and interesting puzzles.

The Fall is certainly a good story, however, it is a dull game. Most of the gameplay revolves around trying to find a single item somewhere on the floor, and then combining it with another item halfway across the map. The combat is no better; once you figure out where to angle your gun, then it becomes ridiculously easy.
The story itself, though, is well done. It explores the behaviour of robots relative to their programming, the nature of rules, and has a few good twists along the way.
Graphics are decent enough. Moving on.
Audio? The voice acting is very good. The music however, is easy to forget. The ambient sounds are nicely done though.
All in all, would be better as a short film.

Machinarium, a point-and-click, third-person adventure game made entirely in flash by a Czech game company.
It's a beautiful world full of robots and mechanical equipment. Even the decaying equipment is beautiful to look at. If you like Myst-style adventures, The Neverhood, or games to test your mind instead of your trigger finger, try this one!
The puzzles are the ideal balance between inventory, environment, and logic. There is no pixel-hunting here--everything you need is out in the open, you just have to decide how to use it. As you progress, the story gradually becomes clear, and your actions have a purpose. The puzzles are fair and make perfect sense. They never feel like contrived devices to delay the player, but are part of the world. Sometimes they're even fun distractions.
As if that weren't enough, the soundtrack is outstanding!
The characters are memorable long after finishing the game. The simple story is fun to discover. The puzzles are challenging, but never unfair. It's the perfect balance of humor, challenge, puzzle and action. Check it out!

Quadrilateral Cowboy unexpectedly became my favorite game in recent years.
I think part of the reason why is that I didn't have very defined expectations. Another reason is that I've been pulled away from longer games simply because of circumstance. So you could say that what Quadrilateral Cowboy actually offered was exactly what I needed at the time of playing it. And what it offers is some of the most subtle, intimate storytelling in gaming intertwined with what I would also call subtle, intimate puzzles. Puzzles with clever solutions but in which the solution is not the most important element.
The highlight of this game is the physicality of the objects you interact with. It is the internal consistency of the tools at your disposal. If it's true that the game never combines all it's elements to present you with truly complicated puzzle challenges (a la Portal, The Witness or Stephen's Sausage Roll), it is also true that the game doesn't really aim for that kind of brainteaser. It has just as much puzzle as is necessary to make you feel in it's world, breaking into things, hacking weird stuff, downoading brain content, sticking it up the corporate overlord. Even though many of the puzzles are  simple, I will never forget how they made me feel. As the story of the three girls progressed, I became part of this rag-tag band of absurd hacker-heros in a way that will stay with me for a long time.
So that's why it has become a most memorable game for me. It is short and sweet. It is subtle and feels profound without posturing or ridiculous gestures of intellectual grandeur (looking at you, Bioshock Infinite). It has great gameplay that you can interact with at the pace of a narrative sensation that encompasses you (never do you need to stop and think for a duration of time in which you are no longer a character and become instead a solver, a detached entity with a notepad and a brain).
It is little escapade into a world I wish existed. And I'm sad it doesn't.

This is a game, at its heart, about starting from nothing and taking over the world. You start with cheap weapons and armor, no friends or followers, and no money. From there, the mechanics point you in the general direction of rallying troops, gathering hero units, conquering land, and gaining experiencing for your hero to forge them from hapless adventurer to steel-clad killing machine. While it is open-world, it's fairly dialogue-light, and most of what there is to do is all about navigating the web of power. If that's your sort of RPG, you'll get a lot of milage out of the single player.
Multiplayer is a little more eh--while it's well balanced and the game modes offer interesting tactical challenges, it can also feel clunky at times. The community can also be a pain--not as bad as some other games, but noticibly annoying at times.

The Good:
- The voice actor who played the system administrator did a phenomenal job.
- Unquestionably, the best parts of this game are the interactions between the ARID and the System Administrator. Their dialogue throughout the game kept me invested and became the only reason I played through to the end.
The Bad:
- As stated, the interactions between ARID and the System Administrator were the best parts of the game. However, the resolution to their story came too abruptly. This gripe was not helped by the unsatisfying conclusion to the game.
- The combat segments did not add anything to the game. In fact, these parts felt like they were just there to extend the length of the game.
- Some of the character animations are really rough. For example, when the main character jumps the transition from the jump position to the standing position is jarring. Moreover, the sluggish controls further expose the rough animations.
- I experienced some bugs during my playthrough which forced me to close out the game and restart.
Final Verdict:
There are some great aspects to this game, but it’s marred by elements which provide no value to the gameplay or story. As a result, I can’t recommend this game. Perhaps, when the story arch is complete it might be worth playing through, but in its current state it’s not worth it. As an aside, the name of this game is too generic and it’s difficult to look up information regarding the second game because of it. At the very least they could have titled it The Fall: I Don’t Know, Something Clever.
A traditional puzzle adventure, hidden in the trappings of a side-scrolling action game. Clever and engaging, with a solid story and well-fleshed out characters. Looking forward to the second one.

Mixed bag. I would only recommend this game to someone who has an appreciation for concept, mood, and other art aspects of games.
The Fall has a great atmosphere. The story and transitions help to draw you into a derelict, distopian world. The voice acting is well done.
Gameplay is mediocre. This game would be ok for casual gamers. Controls are moderately clunky (I used an xbox controller). Gameplay involves looking around rooms to find clues and items to interact with. It is not always clear what to do next, or how to solve the puzzle. Some of the steps required to complete puzzles are rather arbitrary. There are also some interspersed combat sequences. These are fun, but 80% of the fights are not challenging at all, thanks to the cloaking device, which allows you to go untargetable.
The game seriously lacks content. I beat the game in just over 4 hours. (I bet I could do a speedrun in less than half that time.) The Fall should be called "The Fall: Chapter 1". The story, which is so captivating and expertly told, will leave you feeling a bit unsatisfied. Additionally, there is almost no replay-value. The game mechanics give you the illusion of choice and customization with arbitrary dialogue options and "upgrades" that, instead of being used to offer a variety of experiences, only serve to keep the game linear (similar to Tomb Raider 6). So you're basically paying $?.?? for a game you're going to play once for 4 hours. Worth it? You decide. However, what little content they have is decently well done, and supposedly, The Fall 2 is currently under development. If you like a good story and have a little disposable income, go ahead and get it.

Gotta go mothertrucking fast!
A lot of people describe this as a simple concept with an astoundingly solid gameplay. It's fast, its chaotic, and its absolute madness.
Your sole objective is to jump from one truck onto another and avoid falling onto the ground or hitting a wall in a painful way all to reach the goal in the fastest way possible. Now that may sound easy the first few levels in, but later on it gets even more hectic.
The game features a leaderboard system which allows you to compete with other players and friends to see who is the better speedrunner (or glitcher/map breaker), just don't try to become the #1 in a level though, the leaderboards are filled with people who hacked the game to beat the level in 0 seconds just to have their shameful names written over it.
Oh, and the sountrack? The soundtrack is kickass! Suits every world level very well and its catchy enough that you might end up banging your head back forth to the beat. I would from the bottom of my heart recommend buying the soundtrack DLC, its that good, really!
Now the cons of the game... well, the speedrunning is fine and all, but its just that because of the chaotic physics that come in with the game make it so much more luck based, sure if you got the right skills and power-ups you could avoid those, but there is just so many times the physics went haywire and launched me at random directions only that god knows how it happened. Not this is not that big of an issue, the game is purely physics based when it comes to trucks, and really adds a surprise factor all over, and may even generate some intense and pretty sick moments where you jump onto a flying truck and to another, trying to desperately reach the goal without falling to your death.
But overall, the game is really fun to play and would totally recommend buying it when its on sale. And even the soundtrack, just do it!
And remember, stay fast, stay safe, and don't try this at home.

Update: After playing this game I can give a good pro's and cons list:
Pros:
High Speed Aerial 3D combat is great
Characters are interesting
Vareity of weapons allows for a multitude of appraoches
Story is decent enough
Hectic aerial dog fights can be super Fun
Cons:
Camera can be a bit buggy
You can spam funnels and trivialize the game
Everyone speaks over eachother so don't even bother listening to dialouge
Difficulty is simulated by having an enemy you can't keep up with/shoot,being absurdly outnumbered, actual swarms of missiles, or in the case of 2 fights all of the above.
My final Verdict: The game has a ton of potential and is really well done for an early access title BUT still has those EA kinks. If you're a fan of the Aerial part of AC4 definetely pick this up

One of the best, true survival-horror games, ever.
REmake took the original RE1, the game hailed as the beginning of the whole genre, and made it not only (a lot) prettier, but also bigger, smoother and definitely scarier as well. For old RE-fans it offers plenty of all new material and re-designed old features to make the experience fresh again (it's said that up to 75% of REmake is brand new compared to RE1!). For newcomers, there simply isn't a better way to start this magnificent series. Before this re-release, this magnificent gem was a Nintendo Gamecube exclusive.
A word of warning to the generation who's idea of horror / Resident Evil is limited to post-RE4 games and titles like Dead Space: there is action in the old RE games, but this is not an action game. There's weird camera angles, the characters move with the trademark "tank controls" (that are worth mastering!), you cannot move while aiming with a weapon, and you only get just about enough ammo to finish the game. There's also limited saves in form of the ink-ribbons you use on typewriters, that are scattered around the mansion. Most of the game plays like an adventure game of sorts; you run around the fairly huge mansion, first mapping out the place and its features, and try to solve puzzles that would allow you to to proceed further. There WILL be backtracking, item management, and plain head-scratcher moments!
What comes to this "HD" port, it's mostly quite successful. While most of the pre-rendered backgrounds are only re-scaled and photoshop filtered, they still look OK for the most part. There's plenty of animation in many of them, and characters even cast shadows on top of them realistically. The 3D models are pretty much the same as 13 years ago, but they already looked great back then. The new 60fps mode definitely pleases modern players, even if it's real advantages over the default 30 are kinda small; this is NOT a shooter game, after all!
Performance: Any 2010-ish "real" gaming PC should run this HD Remaster flawlessly. My old i5 2500 + 8GB RAM + GTX 560ti 1GB runs the game just great at 1920x1200 resolution, 60fps mode, all settings high. I also have a lower end laptop with i3 @ 2.1ghz, 6GB, GT 540M 1GB, and to my surprise it actually struggles a lot when playing REmake. I had to edit the game's .ini files to get 640x480 resolution, and throw everything on Low, just to get smooth ~30fps. People with integrated videochips certainly won't get enjoyable ride with this port.
tl;dr: Interested in the root of modern horror genre, puzzle solving, or just plain high quality games? Then you NEED to play Resident Evil Remake!

Let me give you a break down. This game looks innocent enough, nice voxel style that everyone is familiar with by now, and the game seems so innocent with it's tutorial setup. That is all a mask that the game pulls off almost as soon as you step into the real game. You start out as a white blob that you have named what ever you want. In my case, I named myself Pigeon Lord to follow my trend of fowl named stuff. I claimed a nice section of the Winter Wasteland biome, but then I found that my realm was not all snowy and beautifully glazed with ice. I found that my land had been struck with a massive case of Global Warming and all the nice winter decor was gone and replaced with a regular forest. I could get around this, if I hadn't decided to look at the upper corner with the little shop section. This game is laced with micro-transactions that seem to make EA look like it is a newcomer to the whole free-to-play section of gaming. The biggest bundle is $20 and gives you 50,000 of the in-game currency. This may seem like a lot at first, considering that mining random blocks has a chance of giving you only 1 Cubit (In-game currency name). The game actually sells some items like the House Pack, which contains some tems for 100 Cubits, but then you get the Almighty Cube Pack which gives you 1x Almighty Cube, and it does NOTHING! The Almighy Cube has no use except to show that you either grinded away until your fingers broke off and then used your nose to play the game, or that you decided to throw more money at Cosmic Cow, and the fact that the pack costs 25,000 Cubits is what makes gamers hate free to plays! This game also has a stunning lack to move the camera downwards from it's skewed angle, making it impossible to make any form of dungeon if you wanted to make a nice Castle RP Realm. The world only likes to look from an angle that makes it even impossible to decide where you want to make a basement for a nice building if you wanted to, for it lacks any sense of the word elevation. If you wanted to make a basement anyways, you would either have to make the walls out of clear glass to be able to see inside, and even then you have to cut out two walls to make sure you can actually make sure your character isn't running straight into a wall all the time. Then we get on the idea of how you would even have enough room for some of the amazing things they show in their screenshots above. The realms that you get are a decent size to build a small amount of stuff, and then end up ripping your heart out when you go to make a nice Bungelow, for the realms only go about 4-5 blocks deep, but if you buy the more expensive, larger ones you might have more space for building underground, or just have to buy enough blocks to build the whole world up and then put in your basement. This game isn't currently worth anyones time, and if you want to try it, then download the 31 mb and wait for the game to find a server, for that is another bug that exists. The game will freak out and not let you even play it's tutorial if it can't find you a server, and it usually take a good 10-15 minutes for the game to realize that you are actually able to connet to one of their servers. Until they fix the pacing of the game and how often the currency drops and if the worlds and camera learn the word elevation, this game isn't even worth the .9 hours I put into it.

As with all older games, the graphics have aged, but they still do their job. It would be nice if it were a little easier to tell some units apart, but overall I can't complain.

I bought this game several years ago. I'm not quite sure why I did but it was on sale and I thought 'why not?'. I got a good 20 or so hours in but the whole time I didn't really know what I was doing. I didn't bother read the rulebook and I was going about the game by feel. Yet somehow... I was having fun. I didn't even bother with the story mode or anything. I just kept setting up games with teams I thought looked cool and had at it!
Fast forwarding to now, I had a strange urge to play Blood Bowl again but this time actually learn how to play. I did the tutorial, read through the rulebook, watched some YouTube videos of people playing the actual board game itself, and played some of the campaign with a nice dwarven team I called "The LIttle D's" with the motto "Our♥♥♥♥♥♥♥are small but so are you!". From what I've seen on the discussions, you will NEED to read the rulebook or else you won't be having much fun here. The game really isn't that hard but there's a slight learning curve that I really think isn't so bad. Now onto the game...
When it comes to core gameplay, it's quite fun! It's essentially just the board game so in the chance you've played and liked Blood Bowl in real life, you'll enjoy this too. After you create a team and really make it your own, you can then play through the campaign or make special matches or whatever. During each individual match, you set up 11 of your guys however you wish. The ball gets kicked and then you and your opponent take turns trying to grab the ball and take it to the end zone to score a point. It's really not that easy though! You'll be constantly moving players around trying find the best position, knocking guys over, pushing through walls of enemies, tossing the ball, and so on. There is an element of chance in there though that forces you to be careful. Each one of your guys may only move once BUT if a 'turnover' occurs then you must immediately end your turn and you'll only get 16 turns total in a game! At eight turns the game resets for it's halftime. For a turnover to occur, you might drop the ball, fail to pick it up, one of your guys gets turned flat on their face, and more. Imagine only moving one guy out of eleven and then your opponment moves all their fellas! That's a massive setback. The risk-management of this game keeps you on your toes. Not only that, who knows what could happen! Maybe one of your guys screws up what should have been an easy task or someone just flat out dies! Gotta go mothertrucking fast!
A lot of people describe this as a simple concept with an astoundingly solid gameplay. It's fast, its chaotic, and its absolute madness.
Your sole objective is to jump from one truck onto another and avoid falling onto the ground or hitting a wall in a painful way all to reach the goal in the fastest way possible. Now that may sound easy the first few levels in, but later on it gets even more hectic.
The game features a leaderboard system which allows you to compete with other players and friends to see who is the better speedrunner (or glitcher/map breaker), just don't try to become the #1 in a level though, the leaderboards are filled with people who hacked the game to beat the level in 0 seconds just to have their shameful names written over it.
Oh, and the sountrack? The soundtrack is kickass! Suits every world level very well and its catchy enough that you might end up banging your head back forth to the beat. I would from the bottom of my heart recommend buying the soundtrack DLC, its that good, really!
Now the cons of the game... well, the speedrunning is fine and all, but its just that because of the chaotic physics that come in with the game make it so much more luck based, sure if you got the right skills and power-ups you could avoid those, but there is just so many times the physics went haywire and launched me at random directions only that god knows how it happened. Not this is not that big of an issue, the game is purely physics based when it comes to trucks, and really adds a surprise factor all over, and may even generate some intense and pretty sick moments where you jump onto a flying truck and to another, trying to desperately reach the goal without falling to your death.
But overall, the game is really fun to play and would totally recommend buying it when its on sale. And even the soundtrack, just do it!
And remember, stay fast, stay safe, and don't try this at home.

Bless their indie little hearts. I'm very impressed, the gameplay is well-thought out with tight(ish) controls and a clear progression in difficulty. It's fun to watch, with lots of missiles and lasers filling up the screen, making evasion and speed very important components of gameplay. Making the player use the Normal mechss and contrasting them to the mobility and lethality and survivability armaments of the hero mechs makes it very clear the difference in their capabilities. If you're a fan of high mobility mech combat, like, say, Armored Core 4, Netsphere, Hawken, or Virtua On, this is right up your alley.
What it does lack is maturity. The devs are clearly massive weeaboos when it comes to story and writing. Everything comes across as a mecha anime aimed towards the 10-16 male crowd that thinks games like Ace Combat are a reflection of military aviation operations. It oozes with angsty teenagers dealing with existentialist and solipsist questions about participating in warfare (in real life, the ethical problem with dealing with child soldiers is that they're TOO good at operating gameified weapons systems, TOO accepting of command structure, and TOO willing to dehumanize the enemy, where their competency is deepy tied to identity, Full Metal Panic and Gundam 00 do this well).
The game slowly rolls out new missions, which is nice. I'd like to see it roll back to polish over some of the rough spots with difficulty balancing, some context to using the laser sword (which is supposed to be used for CIWS but it doesn't really work) and the lock-on camera. Right now the bullet time feature is an orphaned mechanic, it doesn't help with swording down missiles and it doesn't help aim the rifles. It might be useful for missile lockon management or situational awareness, but for the most part, I'm not sure why it's there.
Overall, the game is very unpolished and the devs seem very young. But it's heaps of fun and fills a niche that FromSoft left unfilled when they buried Armored Core to makes more Souls games, Zone of the Enders is never coming back, and all the Gundam games seem to be focused on ground-based combat in the One-Year's War.
I'm buying whatever game these devs make next, but this one is a solid amateur effort that's good for a few hours of weeblord fun.

This is a review for an Early Access game, therefore opinions therein are subject to change and be edited as new updates roll out for the game. By all accounts this is not a final review of any form for the game, but instead a review of the current build, which will continually be updated per update, etc.
Project Nimbus has managed to capture the seemingly difficult gameplay of the Armored Core series, and transfer it to the PC-verse. The game is fun, but immensely frustrating due to specific enemies. Let's go ahead and get on to the pros and cons, shall we?
Pros:
- Native Support of a large array of resolutions up to 2560x1440 (Also 2560x1080 with some fiddling here and there).
- Extremely fast-paced and open-world combat, resulting in high speed shootouts and air brawls.
- Very engaging soundtrack, with perfectly crafted music for intense fights, as well as moments within the story where you feel tasked with something almost insurmountable.
- Stylish "Battle Frames" (Mecha), that potentially change per mission.
- An interesting Storytelling aspect, where you change factions every few missions.
- Relatively interesting Storyline, detailing the conflicts between several of the worlds leading factions.
- Evolving Storytelling, and new story aspects as the game is being developed, such as newly fleshed out ideas, Audio Logs related to the Battle Frame Pilots conversing between one another in some missions, and so on.
- Survival Mode is a breath of fresh air. Survival Mode allows you to select one of the many Battle Frames within the game that you may/may not be able to pilot during the normal storymode. Things such as the S47 Berkut, and Col. Andei's Customized Terminator make an appearance here, with the lower, non-overpowered Frames having very high score multipliers as compensation for their lack of utility skills/sheer main weaponry power.
Cons (These may be due to the game being in Early Access, so my review will be edited as time goes on and the game progresses more).
- Horrible support for controller, even though it's seemingly within the game. This is due to the games large amount of buttons required for gameplay, which work flawlessly on keyboard.
- Maneuverability of Battle Frames leaves something to be desired. This game won't have you being killed by enemies most times, but instead due to wrestling with the clunky and lackluster maneuverability of the Battle Frame. Boosting doesn't provide enough distance, as well as there being no dedicated dodging left, right, forward, or back, thus resulting in you using your primary acceleratory boost to dodge in specific directions, which does not work well whatsoever. Prepare for an incoming runthrough of running into objects, not being able to descend correctly, and so on.
- Flares don't work. There are moments where Flares (Designed to divert enemy missiles) will work, and times where they will not. Letting enemies launch missiles directly at me within the game, popping flares and then dodging in the same situation every time will result in the flares working about 20% of the time to draw enemy missiles, however in some early missions they seem to work almost flawlessly.
- The inability to customize Frames before departing on a mission (In the story), this seems on purpose, however a very large aspect of Mecha brawlers is the customization, allowing players to take on tasks that they otherwise would not be able. Luckily there's an array of weapons at your disposal on MOST Battle Frames.
- Sword Combat is extremely flawed in that it only propels you forward, not towards an enemy in any way even when locked on, which a game like this in an open-world 3D environment requires.
- Internal/External object collision. Once more, this goes hand in hand with the maneuverability aspects, resulting in indoor combat being a hot mess.
Overall, for the Early Access version of the game, I'd give it a 7/10. It's missing polish, and some control tweaks, but it's satiated that mecha brawler craving I've had ever since I stopped playing Armored Core: Verdict Day.

Developed by Brendon Chung, the master storyteller behind Gravity Bone and Thirty Flights of Loving, Quadrilateral Cowboy is the next chapter in Blendo Games’ series of titles set in a retro futuristic world of portable vinyl players, flying motorbikes and morally dubious protagonists. The big difference between Quadrilateral Cowboy and its predecessors, however, is that it’s a fully functional game, with clearly defined objectives and gameplay mechanics, instead of the “walking simulator” approach employed by the developer with his earlier work.
Brendon Chung’s latest title is an adventure game disguised as a puzzle-solving experience. We play as a recently graduated engineer dabbling in computer hacking and engaging in a series of high stakes heists. From the beginning of the game, we can see that Quadrilateral Cowboy’s world diverged from ours at some point, as it’s set in the 1980s, but there are flying motorbikes and VR seems to be a fully functional thing. Computers must still be controlled through DOS-like interfaces though, something that fits the cyberpunk theme perfectly, and adds a tactile dimension to our interactions with the game world.
The beginning of the adventure will teach players how to hack doors and other objects in the game world, using a portable hacking deck that must be deployed and then interacted with. The act of hacking feels real thanks to the use of believable commands typed on the portable computer’s miniature keyboard and displayed on its screen, and after a few small “test” levels, most gamers will be typing commands as if they were real life hackers.
Quadrilateral Cowboy is quite similar to Portal, introducing a new gadget, building a level around the use of that tool and then seamlessly adding it to the player’s arsenal as a thing that may or may not be used to complete later puzzles. This is usually something good, but at some points it feels like the first half of the game is a tutorial for the latter part of the adventure. Luckily, the story is intriguing enough to carry the “tutorial” parts, and the strangeness of the environments ensures that the player never feels bored, even with the most basic tasks.
Between each mission, we’ll be taken to playable intermissions which usually take only a few seconds (though the player can always explore the environment at their leisure) and through those scenes we can learn more about the world, our character and her friends/associates. For instance, we can discern that even though our character is a recently graduated engineer, the city of Nuevos Aires has no need for her skills (or her friends’ skills) and that’s the reason for her criminal activities.
As the game progresses, the plot’s pace quickens, the stakes are higher and we get to play through complex levels that make use of all the gadgets acquired along the way. Sadly, not everything is perfect, as Quadrilateral Cowboy seems to be a quite buggy piece of software (picking up gear in order to stash it may trigger crashes for no apparent reason) and some players may feel that the duration of the game is a problem (I got through the game in four hours) Still, even with those caveats, I believe that Blendo Games’ latest adventure is one of the most enjoyable titles of 2016, and I can’t wait to see what Brendon Chung’s got planned for the future.

Fable is the classic action rpg by lionhead studios, and can be described as a box of toffee. It takes a while to get through, its enjoyable in the moment, but by the end you feel ill and the experience isn't memorable in any way.
The plot is as standard as it gets with fantasy stories. Your home town is burned down by baddies and you spend the rest of your life training to become a powerful warrior to stop the bad guys and help or hurt people. That is literally the entire plot in a sentence, there are no surprises in all honesty, or unique elements outside of the ability to be "evil" or "good". Even then, the being evil or good options boil down to "want to be a complete♥♥♥♥♥♥" or "want to be the goody two shoes?". There are some mildly amusing side quests, but almost all of them have been done better in other rpgs.
The combat is pretty bog standard as well. You have melee (which is mainly one handed weapons, no shields, duel wielding), long range (bows and crossbows, which handle more or less the exact same), and magic (which has about 20 spells). The melee is simple, mash attack, use a guard break move when the enemy blocks, occasionally block or dodge, repeat. You will win 90% of fights this way without much issue. Range is basically useless unless you are fighting flying enemies, or if you want to pick off one or two enemies from a distance before they swarm you. Magic begins as tiny♥♥♥♥♥magic missiles, but can get really OP if you invest time into it. It never felt challenging, and I routinely did the "no armour" boast on quests just to add some level of difficulty. (I'll get to that in a bit.)
Outside of combat, you can do gestures, this ranges from farting and burping, to pickpocketing and laughing like a♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ They all have their uses, but you don't really need to bother with them for the most part unless you are trying to get a wife (which can be almost anyone), or want to make people run away so you can steal from stores. You can have sex if you want, and you can break the game by buying and renting property to generate infinite gold. But ultimately, alot of the things you can do outside of combat feel pointless, they are there, and its nice that you can do these sort of things which means you can be whatever kind of person you want to be. But they feel like pointless fluff.
That goes for most of the game actually. Alot of it feels pointless, as if the people writing this just didn't care at all, save for some dialog here and there, the way this game was written feels as bland and generic as it gets. Even the boast system on quests (one of the only actually good systems in the game) feels tacked on. You can take any quest from the guild you want, and boasts on top of that, in order to gain greater renown and more money. But its far easier to just farm the renown from enemies out in the world and get the money from renting out houses.
Graphically speaking, it’s an older title, so it gets a pass on looking a bit dated, if anything it has aged well given how cartoonish everything looks. The music however is as forgettable as everything else though, not a single song really sticks out in my mind.
Overall, this game was a disappointment. I beat this game on the Xbox a while back, and replayed it here, and I forgot how lacking this title was in, well, anything. I can't recommend it to rpg fans who want choices, because none of their choices really make a difference. I can't recommend it to any action rpg fans either, since there are far better titles like witcher 2 which do everything this game does but far better. It has no deep or thought provoking story to speak of either, so its more of a waste of time than anything. If you are looking for a quick, easy rpg fix without having to worry about micro managing anything, and don't care that the game has little depth, then you might want to pick this up and play it while you wait for another real rpg get your hands on.

Others would say this game is a good one, but I say, nope.
Here's why:
RNG is not random at all.  There's no random anything, because I've seen dice rolls before, for this game on table top, and they aren't nearly this one sided even in the worst of cases (mini wargaming has videos with them playing this table top version, and even then they aren't nearly this bad).
Difficulty setting?  No reason to lie, its hard, extra hard, might as well not play.  Actually, I'm wrong, it goes: don't bother, don't bother, don't bother.
No change to difficulty changes any part of the game.  Meaning that you put it on easy?  It's still going to bend you over, put it on hard, it still, guess what, bends you over.  They make dodge after dodge, gfi after gfi, single dice blocks and double against and nothing happens.  The player?  First dodge fails, or second dodge fails (I haven't done double dodge moves because of this), single dice blocks are attacker down 90% of the time, rerolled into attacker down or both down, and double against?  Might as well buy another player at that point.
This is the worst case of RNG I have seen in a game, in forever.  There's no reason the dice couldn't be actually ballanced or the rolls be actually random.
I wouldn't buy anything from this dev, so long as it's a game that's supposedly an adaption of a table top game.  Since they have BB2, and the reviews are down right ugly for that game, I will not be purchasing or playing this game again.
And if you've gotten this far, and wonder how someone could say such things about this game without playing it for a while?  Look at how many hours I've logged, and you can see I have given this game way more time than it actually deserves.
1/10.  The one is for graphics, since these, although clunky and weird at times, do make the game look semi nice.
I urge you, as a final note, not to get this game if you haven't already, and if you have, don't get BB2, you can read their reviews and see the issues, but lets face it, they took a turd, polished it, and handed it back to you...  What's that saying?  Polish a turd, its still a turd?

I also can’t deny that the anime art style, dating sim, somewhat Japanese influence, and sexual content did assist in enticing me, but regardless of what made me play the game it was the puzzle aspect that kept me playing.  Let’s face it, there are easier ways to see the handful of hentai pics in this game and if you really just want those and somehow can’t find them on Google, purchasing the Art Collection DLC (yes it exists) will net you all those photos and more for a handful of dollars, which is much cheaper than the 10 hours I put in to complete the game.  If you get hooked, there’s a lot more game to enjoy as you are never limited on how many times you can date the girls afterward, there’s a harder “alpha” mode you can begin after successfully sleeping with all the girls (including the unlockable secret ones), and an odd male/female track decision at the beginning that doesn’t change the sex of the people you are romancing but does offer different key art to unlock.  I’m sad to say that the full blown addiction didn’t set in and after about 15 hours my need to consistently start up HuniePop and go on a date or two has subsided, but that’s not to say I don’t jump in every now and again for a game or two when I have 20 minutes to kill.  You’re going to take some flack for it, but if you want a new take on a classic model, HuniePop might be worth your time.

I waited a little to review this. Got a few hours under my belt of playing so I guess it's a good time.
What makes this game fun?
-Guns. Lots of guns. For lack of better description, it's diablo with guns set in a apocalyptic world.
-Unintentional Humor. The poor translating of the game text has caused for some hilarious quotes from NPCs.
-Community. The number of people playing isn't huge which could be a negative, if it didn't cause for creating a very tight nit like community where a lot of people know each other and know of each other causing the game to feel more friendly and rewarding to log onto. It's kind of like that bar in Cheers. You want to go where everybody knows your name.
-Music. The soundtrack for the game is actually pretty good. I enjoy it a lot.
What makes the game kinda hard/boring/ maybe bad?
-Grindy. While I don't mind, some people might find the game grindy and boring because of it. Once you hit level 50 you kind of run out of quests to do and have to grind dailies and just mobs to get xp to get to the cap level of 60. Kinda rough, but some people actually enjoy this.
-Limitation to your character. Nobody really tells you when you start to watch how you spend your skill points because when you want to respec, you will have to pay real money or start over new character. Well now you know, so maybe it takes one bad thing away.
-Outdated Graphics. Once again, something that doesn't bother me, but might others. A lot of people seem to voice concern of the graphics looking similiar to that of the original Diablo, which can be said they are poor and outdated. However in the time and age of nostalgia, where people are playing 8 bit games on super gaming PCs and not complaining, this seems like a♥♥♥♥♥♥poor excuse to complain about a game.
Overall. This game is super fun and can get you hooked if you're into this style of games. At the same time, it's not a cup of tea for everyone to share, so give it a try and see if you enjoy the sip.

On a serious note, this MMORPG is unlike your usual ones.  At first, seeing the game trailer and screenshots and looking at the review score, I was immediately turned off by how gimmicky yet another F2P game on Steam seems, and I never would have wanted to touch it were it not for my friend who requested we play it.
Upon a glance it may seem like a third-rate cheap budget game but it has a unique engine unlike anything I've seen before. It's 2.5D and it also has physics (dead bodies and loose objects can interact physically against terrain of the world), and I've never seen any engine reproducing any aspects of physics in any MMO, but this one does it well. I believe this game is newly released based off a Korean company and it has some ways to go but it's a very promising and solid game as it stands which is fun to play with friends, at least for a while.
It's basically a very funky and "strange" game with many weird unconventional things but you can still easily see the effort and love that the developers seem to have put into the game. The art is astounding, and world models varying based on your equipped items, which is more than some free MMOs can ask for. The translation is absolutely horrible and grammatically always incorrect in every single line of text but is still so easily understandable and thus humorously lovable.
I recommend a shot at this game if you're having a hard time deciding. This is one of those "wtf" games that you can't stop laughing at yet relaxingly enjoy with friends.

TL;DR: Gameplay is good, but the missions, backstory and design need some polish. Oh and some originality would be nice too.
So there are not many mech games for the PC. Good ones especially. Well, here's some hope for you.
Project Nimbus is basically Another Century's Episode mixed with Ace Combat. But, if you thought that this would be a pale imitation of those 2, well, you might be a bit wrong.
Controls aren't especially tight, but that's probably a good thing since most levels are open airspaces. The mobility of the mechs invokes Armored Core 4/For Answer's feel, where you actually can somehow feel the momentum of the frames as you slow down from a full boost.
Battles often feel like a 3D bullet hell game (yes, I'm looking at you, fake Arkbird) so you'll have to dodge in all 3 axes of movement so to avoid becoming Swiss cheese. You also have flares too to avoid missiles. The main draw of this game is definitely the hectic and very much fast-paced combat. You'll be rushing towards effective range, dodging missiles, maneuvering yourself away from the enemy fire and trying your best to shoot down your foe in all the same time. The developer was even generous enough to program a button to slow down the action so you can observe the eye candy, which may include an Itano circus, lasers and other tropes common in mech anime and video games.
The music is very nice to hear too, but the voice acting was somewhat a hit and miss. While there may be many references towards many other titles in this genre (3x faster tropes, funnels and whatnot referencing Gundam), however originality is a bit at stake here. One mission was probably directly ripped off from Ace Combat 5 (see: White Bird part 1), which was made worse by the fact that they did not bother to change the names of some of the vehicles as well as the mission pacing.
Despite the issues above, I enjoyed the game very well and look forward to what the devs can put in the final product.

This is a Yes + No review, I'm in the middle on this one.
The gameplay is actually quite fun, even though it can get a bit monotonous at times. The mechanics/movement is not great, nor is it bad, it's perfectly decent. The feel when you shoot someone or get shot is also quite decent. The maps are well built, allow diversity and are a lot of fun. Since it's free i'd advise you to simply download it and test it.
However, it takes ages to move up in rank if you don't pay2play. It also takes AGES to save up enough money to upgrade / buy new weapons. And since you need rank in order to get more maps, you end up grinding the same maps with the same weapons for a lot of time.
Of course they want to make money so you should pay em a bit, I would if I could. I do however think that the currency you buy for real money is way to expensive. 20euroes won't get you far, which imo would be a good price for the game overall.
To conclude: It's worth downloading and trying, kinda fun at times, so go ahead and give it a shot.

The Impossible Game is a short but challenging platforming-type game where you control a cube trying to make it through the end of an obstacle course full of pits, spikes, and non-existant gravity.
This is a very fun game, and that's primarily because of it's difficulty and great soundtrack. All you can do is jump. The only thing to aid you is the sound of the music as the soundtrack mostly goes with the course. You'll die again and again, but you'll keep coming back for more because you want to beat that stage, and hear the entire song. You get an amazing feeling of satisfaction when you accomplish it, let me tell you. It's a test of your memory and reflexes. Play to win.
The game's length can depend on how good you are, but the level selection is rather short. It's only 5 levels long, and the length of each stage is around 2 minutes. The replay value comes to just simply beating the level. The only other thing you can do is create levels of your own in the level editor. If you like that kind of thing, then by all means, go for it.
Overall, The Impossible Game is an addicting, very hard game with a very upbeat soundtrack. If you love challenge and reflex games, then buy this. If that's not your cup of tea, you might not find much enjoyment out of it.

Highly Disapointed.  Where to begin?  On the lower levels, the game is way to easy. It will even sometimes on its next movet decide to cover the same bishop again.  Also early in the game, I capture the computers Queen with mine.  My Queen is not covered.  This is known as a Queen Trade.  When I capture the computer's Queen, stading next to the computer's King, the King runs away?  I used to teach Chess to kids as young as 4 years old; otherwise you'd hear me say, I have never seen that.  On the highest level, the computer takes several minutes to make a move.  When the 7th move was exceeding 10 minutes, I quit the game.
When you get into the different modes that it offers, it becomes kind of a joke.  There are two options for combat Chess.  IF you're good at Guitar Hero, you'll probably do well with the Duel part.  When the arrow key lines up in the circle, press the arrow key.  Do so successfully, and you'll begin to do damage to the piece you are fighting against.  In some ways, this part was done well;  but its not Chess.  IF you are attacked, you can defend your square, and make the attacking piece retreat, and have its health reduced.  When you go to capture a piece, win the combat and you get the square.  Lose and you stay where you are.  After about 4 games of this, I got good at it.  Now, I can advance a pawn straight up the field, taking each square as I go, and stopping the computer pieces from harming me.  I was able to Checkmate the king in 4 moves as I moved the Kings pawn straight up the field, put him in Check, and though the pawn wasnt covered by any piece, I beat the King in combat, and won the game.
The graphics I think are good, if not a little predictable and repetitive.  You'll be sick of the repetitive battle music after 4 games, and the lack of additional "Chess Sets"  is kind of disappointing.  Thought the intrusive DRM problems that everyone was writing about were going to be a problem.  Instead, after playing the game for about 2 days, I'm basically done with it. Setting sail for uncharted waters! Destination: Blood Bowl – Legendary Edition. Referee paid! Beer? Bought! Secret Weapons for the sidelines? Activated! So this is a Warhammer game huh? Okay. But….it is about football! Well, not exactly Football. More like Blood Bowl! This game is really a tactics game with a lot of layers of tactical shenanigans you can get up to if you 1) understand them 2) take time to think about it. The game presents itself as a “favorite sport of orcs, elves and other warhammer races” kind of a turn based sport themed tactical game of quite the challenging difficulty and satisfying gameplay:
There are announcers in the game, they comment on certain moves, mistakes and outcomes of the game. The music is really well done. Camera controls are perfect and the game creates a nice atmosphere of actually standing at the sidelines and commanding your werewolf runners to “blitz that puny elf out or I’ll gut you like chickens after the game” *coughcough* I mean…you feel drawn into the game at a satisfying level. For me at least that was the case. In a good way.
You don´t have to be a sports game fan to like blood bowl, but it might tip the scales in you favour if you are. If you are into complex rules behind a pretty straightforward game concept (meaning you can just start playing and get better with each game)  then Blood Bowl serves your cravings. If you like Warhammer as a theme, it is a bonus. Not necessary!
Cargo!  It is a game that you have to invest some time into to get the rules and figure out your own tactics. It is really not for in-between. So for me, due to lack of time, I will have to wait until I touch this solid tactics game again. But I will. Definitely. And then I might even try the RTS Mode that exists!

‘The Fall’ is a decent little puzzle game, with a few issues but great atmosphere. At ten bucks, for less than three hours of gameplay, it is a bit pricey though.
The visuals and the overall style are the game’s greatest strength, giving it depth and personality which can also by expanded upon with the different little pieces of information one can extract from the story here and there.
There are a few flaws, -I already mentioned the rather steep price tag for such a short game-, but the combat is another one for example since it feels rather clumsy. But then again, the controls in general are a little bit wonky. I can understand that this is plot-related but when you are expected to fight enemies with those mechanics, it gets a little bit in the way. The inventory system and the interactions with the environment could be improved too. It is rather fidgety to access certain highlights of the background, and while the style of the game is very nice to look at, seeing every intractable object in the dark is rather difficult.
They are three acts, and the second one is the weakest in my opinion, as it basically locks you in a room with eight different puzzles to solve. It feels very specific to video games and not to the narrative as a whole. By that, I mean that these puzzles could fit anywhere, they almost exist in a sort of vacuum, disconnected from the rest of the game. Although, since to solve the puzzle, you have to interact with other puzzles to resolves them, it is a bit more interesting than it would seem at first glance. Furthermore, there a few notes here and there to remind you of the game you are playing, so it really is just a very minor personal grievance of mine.
Overall, I enjoyed my time with the game, mostly for the intriguing setting, with an oppressing and disturbing atmosphere. I’m curious about the next bit, where will this go now? Perhaps it might be best to wait for the second part to come out and buy both of them in a package though.

This game has a lot of potential.  There are many enjoyable aspects to the game, and my opinion overall is positive.  That being said there are also a few things that could be changed.
PROS:
The graphics in the game are good for several reasons:  The textures are detailed enough for instant visual identification of friends and enemies in combat, the lighting is very good, and visual effects are excellent.  The gameplay is different enough to be interesting and based on rank, skillset, equipment aquisition and upgrade, and in-game activity based progressions.  The maps are detailed enough to easily become lost.  Gameplay occurs in several modes from grunt infantry encounters through to strategic play as a commanding general.  The skill, equipment, and rank progression systems are deeply integrated into the game.  Although real money (purchases with "gold") can be used to upgrade your soldiers, it can be expensive.  Napkin backed quick calculations showed that $100 US dollars would not advance a grunt very far at all, limiting the possibility of a noob purchasing their way to victory.  This will be even more important if the game moves from free to play to purchase to play.
CONS
The game engine is sluggish as a... slug.  Attempting to move, stop, aim, and fire was like watching a slow motion movie.   I am sure this will improve as my soldier advances in skill, and as the engine matures.  I felt that I was playing in mollases.   The color balance in the graphics makes it difficult to spot enemies with any certainty.  While a human has no "radar" in reality, they do generally have a powerful sense of spacial relations.  Since we are in a game engine and not the real world, most games address this with some sort of position indication such as a radar or threat display.  This is lacking in the game.  While the skill based progression is fairly balanced, my experience was that it takes FOREVER to rise past level 2 or 3 due to the various interlocking skills require.  As one final note:  The average soldier fielded in WWII was generally able to aim and fire their weapon proficiently before they were allowed to enter combat (except perhaps the USSR early in the war.)
This is a good game with a lot of potential.  Thank you to the developers for making it available as a F2P on steam while it is in early access.

Grey Cubes is a fun brick-breaker with a multitude challenges to keep things interesting.  Bricks can be influenced by a variety of things, including physics, platforms that rise and fall, whirlwind portals that teleport the ball, exploding bricks, and more!
Like any good brick-breaker, there are bonuses that randomly appear as you destroy things, and these bonuses can both help or hinder you along the way.  ALL bonuses are timed, and none of them will result in an instant-kill (I'm looking at YOU, DX-ball!)
There are 60 levels and 13 achievements to be had, although you'll need to play through twice in order to get them all.  One note:
- Despite the description, this isn't based on time; it's based on playing levels.  Play 100 levels to gain this one, but I recommend NOT replaying any levels until you've gotten this one, as replaying levels not only won't go towards the total, it will negatively-affect the level-counter.
Despite the monotone palate, I recommend this game for any fan of the genre.

I don't usualy do reviews, much less wall of texts but this game is just too good to not do it so here it goes, pardon me if it isn't a good review:
Gameplay:
2 Acts, each containing around 5-7 missions (iirc), some of which are multi part and the end stage missions for Act 2 can take up to an entire afternoon to clear, and on top of that there is a survival mode that allows one to choose from any of the in-game mech to play with for additional replayability or just to simply blow stuff up
Controls are a bt hard to get used to initially but once used to it it becomes quite ok actually.
Storyline:
Starts off rather slowly but progresses along quite well, with the ability to play from both side of the conflict s (the CFN and the UCN) in different stages of the same mission, although character development could be stronger- It's only in the 2nd half of act 2 do the MC of both faction start to display emotions and ask questions about the war, the killing etc, with a final feels trip ending in act 2
Music:
No complains there- the opening theme that greets you is absolutely stunning and the rest of the tracks, they resemble what you'll expect from any good mecha series anime. Sound acting is not bad as well althought nothing to worth noting about though
Visuals:
My rig can only take up to high so I can't comment for very high options. While the terrain details are not the best, especially for urban maps, it is more than made up for in the combat scenes when your own unit starts spamming missiles and funnels and bullets.
Overall verdict, it's a great game considering that it's still in early access, can't wait to see how this game will develop considering that there is still a lot of room for development in many aspects such as the story, the chara development and also, the possibility of multiplayer and mech customisation

I played Gravity Bone and Thirty Flights of Loving and loved those games, but be warned, this isn't like them! I really enjoyed the craziness of the other games and that it left me questioning what I had just played, but this is more of a well... fleshed out game, not like the others. The hacking aspect is interesting, but more often than not i found myself just getting fustrated rather than enjoying the game. As much as I was looking forward to playing this because of my love for the other Blendo games, I can't reccomend it.

TL;DR the game feels half done.
The mechanics are great and make for interesting puzzles but don't always expand on the concepts: the first half of the game pretty thoroughly explores the use of your deck (which is more command line interface than programming), but the second half seems to only scratch the surface of the multiple heister possibilities before giving you all the abilities on one character anyways. Multiple weevers, or using the weever and autocase simultaneously, are never explored even though the tools and commands hint at the possibility. Workshop support really SHOULD make up for some of these flaws, but six months later only a handful of levels even exist.
The plot and backstory stuff feels like it's building up to something big, but it never gets there which is unusual given the developer's past works. The game does a good job of establishing the basics of who these people you're playing as are in between levels, but there's never a moment where these relationships are tested or a true antagonist emerges. Some really cool things happen, and then they just stop happening.

On a technical level the game runs fine, but a couple of level breaking bugs forced me to close and reopen the game in order to reattempt the level.
After the reputation built up from Gravity Bone and Thirty Flights of Loving, I was just expecting more than the game gave me. If you're a puzzle fanatic and just want to tool around with some interesting mechanics, then by all means go for it. If you're expecting this to grab your attention in any other way, move on.

1 - Capcom could fix the " cutscenes slowdown/drift sync" (with audio and subtitles comming late, because video slowdown on cutscenes) wich happens with some slower (not so slow...) machines.
2 - To read a file is not a smooth process, when you want to browse fast the pages. The feedback could be reduced, so the pages could be "turned" faster with the "action" or "right" button. And the animation of the text passing from right to left, could be more smoother.
3 - Same issues of damage detection cooldowns that we had on gamecube version. When you fire a shotgun, hit a zombie, or a hunter and it falls on the ground; if you fire again when it's getting up, there's a high chance that this hit doesn't do any damage, as if the targed was "immune" during the animation of getting up - wich I called the "damage vulnerability cooldown".
4 - The mouse arrow should not be visible on the screen. Actually, the idea of making the left mouse button the default attack button, was really bad, since you really don't need a mouse to play the game.
5 - The attack and investigate buttons should be the same. No need to separate them in 2 different buttons. This just makes things more complicated, even more when you want to customize the controls, to stop using the mouse, that I mentioned earlier. Also, a "cancel" button should had been added. It's awful having to hit the "esc" button many times on the menu/inventory operations, when your hands are relaxed over the "w/s/a/d" region of the keyboard.
6 - It would be so utopic to have the old GSc remade as well? Like the draining swiming pool one, the fountain, and the others..? In fact, some locations, seem to have the old resolution from gamecube version, like some sreens near the stairs and water control room (near the sharks)...
7 - Very unfamiliar and non-intuitive system to save the changes done when you alter the control configurations... (you have to hit enter, esc, click on "resume game" and not esc again... so...) This just could be more simple.
8 - The game is wonderful and brings back many good memories... Oh, the achievement page here on steam needs some repairs... It seems to be unfinished/glitchy.
Thank you for reading my comments. A guy who played and finished the original game, in 1996, with eyes closed, with the time of "1:11:27". Despite of the "issues" I reported on this review, Capcom, you did an awesome job! Thank you for bringing to us again this masterpiece!

I really enjoy playing DCUO. I've been a big Batman fan since I was a kid and this allows me to run through Gotham city, interacting with iconic characters that I grew up loving!
This game allows you to pick your side and choose one of the three iconic heros/villains of the DC world to mentor with. I often play a villain with the Joker being my mentor. Whoever mentor's you ends up being your primary contact throughout the game, giving you missions and things to do. You will also work with the other two iconic mentors from time to time, completing missions for them related to their own portion of the DC world.
There's a ton of stuff for you to do as a free member and with a membership, you unlock all of the DLC packs and a bunch of other goodies as well. Plus, with All Access from SOE, you end up getting access to all of the other SOE games too. All in all, it's really a lot of fun to play and I'd highly suggest it as something you can do in your free time that won't require a ton of dedication like a lot of other MMORPGs.

The F2P side does have a lot to offer, though most people don't realize it or lose interest in the grind. The level cap is at 30 yes, but once there, it doesn't really matter. Your combat rating, determined by your gear, is what counts and gives you access to higher tier instances/raids. DLCs vital to gameplay and further advancement would have to be Battle for Earth, Lightning Strikes, and Fight for the Light, in that order. Earth gives you access to higher tier armour after reaching a 45-48 CR as well as a raid... if I recall correctly. Lightning Strikes gives you duos and access to central city, and Light gives you several alerts... though with all the DLCs out now and all future releases, it's hard to keep up with paying for it all, back then I'd say buy the DLCs, seeing as you get to keep them all even without a paid subscription, but becoming a "Legendary" (paid sub) member, is probably the better choice, seeing as your cash flow isn't restricted, nor is your inventory and bank storage space. All that technical stuff aside, DC is great for those who want to jump in on the DC Universe, or are long time fans. Controls really are innovative and I have yet to find another MMO playstyle like it. The combat isn't just a point and click and each class/playstyle is reliant on the other when it comes to PVP. Though it does take some time to get used to the pay off is usually worth the grind, with all the flashy and powerful gear, it'll sate all of your comicbook/gamer needs all in one fell swoop.
Takes a while to get used/good at, but quite fun once you do. Also villain players are much better people than heroes.

TL;DR    Buy if $5 or less for casual players looking for a quick game. $10 or less if you're a puzzle/sci-fi fan.
The Look: The Fall has a cool art style that doesn't get tired on the eyes. Given, it's a pretty short title, but all the same. It won't blow you away, but it definitely serves its purpose. I would suggest, howerever, that you actually turn UP the brightness a bit. The extreme low light caused me to miss quite a few clues and a frustrating 5-15 minutes of backtracking and aimless wandering ensued each time.
The Feel: The game handles OK. There's an awkward switch when you turn around with your pistol drawn that takes a bit of getting used to. If you're used to a high sensitivity mouse, you're going to want to turn that way down as it can become quite unwieldy and cause your character to spasm back and forth from left to right when your pistol is out, which it will be, at all times. There isn't a lot of platforming so the precision of the controls isn't an issue.
The Play: This is where I take my biggest issue with the game. I'm not new to puzzle games, but this game had me check a walkthrough three times (or aimlessly clicking on things to see if it worked). Most of the puzzles are pretty easy... if you have all the things you need. However, as I mentioned above, it is pretty easy to miss key items, completely stalling you in progress. Also, you have the same options for every interaction in the game, but most are simply text blurbs that tell you something. There is never a clear distinction if you can pick up/turn on/shoot/push an item until you've cycled through your entire inventory of options and items. The time I spent checking to see if I could X on icon Y is far too high. A bit of streamlining in this regard would do nicely.
The Story: It's an intriguing game and the story is certainly the highlight. A bit slow to start, it begins to take form and draw you in. It may be a tired scenario; you wake up in a strange place where strange things have happend. You're only sure of one thing, you need to do X. This isn't a knock on the game, it does this little tale admirably. It has twists and turns that may not have avid mystery lovers jumping from their chairs, it will encourage some thinking and pondering about important questions of ethics, morals, and humanity.
Ultimately, I got this game on a sale and did my one playthrough. It didn't wow me and it didn't make me regret buying it. I most likely will not be buying the next chapters though.

Oh boy, this f#cking game. I must be honest, all I knew about this game is that it was violent, and that I had played a demo around 8 or so years ago. And well, seeing it with a big sale like that, I couldn't really hold it and decided to buy it. Is it bad? Is it good? As usual I'm gonna start talking about what it does worse, then move up from there.
First and foremost, the worst part of the game has to be it's difficulty for new players. It's a board game of sorts directly ported to a video-game... But as it usually happens, good board games are complex as all hell, and that translates poorly for new players. It also doesn't help that the difficulty spike is directly at the start: you create your own team and then suddenly you're thrusted with little knowledge of how to play against teams that actually DO HAVE QUITE THE LEVEL ALREADY. Your team will be on a sick losing spree from the beggining because, even though the game says there's around 140 or so teams on the game, you'll be playing against the same mid-level ones over and over. If I start on a 0 prestige league, WHY THE HELL PUT MID-GAME TEAMS ON IT, EVEN ON THE LOWEST DIFFICULTY!? IT'S STUPID. However that's switched around later, when your team actually gets levels and becomes decent, the enemies are actually rather easy to predict.
The second other problem this game has is actually related to that one, too. Remember when I talked about this game being a board-port with tons of rules? Well, this game has a tutorial that last around 10 minutes and all it does is teach you how to move characters, knocking people into the ground and the bare minimum to start playing. It's kinda pathetic when the game has so many damn rules and can be so damn challenging and outright painful to play for new players. The worst part of it all is that I did a bit of research online, and on the Steam forums some people say that to understand the game correctly you gotta read the manual, and also giving a link to a PDF file of said manual... WHICH HAD OVER 50 BIG PAGES OF RULES. WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥. IT'S A F#CKING VIDEOGAME, NOT A SCIENCE PROJECT!
Taking that aside, though, what do we have left? A really fun and adicting game, once you actually learn what the f#ck you're doing.
The gameplay, after you learn about it and get over the start difficult spike, is fun as all hell. Now sure it feels lame when the enemy team pulls off something completely stupid that somehow works, like a ball carrier somehow dodging three players and scoring a touchdown, but all races have their own advantages and styles of play. Wood elfs for example are great at doing large passes and evading blocks, however they just S#CK at melees and end up with multiple injured and DEAD players at them. On the other hand you have guys like the Orcs and Dwarfs, who are violent and while not having much control over the ball, can just win by injuring and killing other players. IT'S LIKE MADDEN MIXED WITH WARHAMMER, ONLY ACTUALLY FUN!
Talking about races, there's like 30 or even more of them, lost count. That's A LOT of variety, I'm pretty confident anyone can find a race that fits their playstyle, me actually going Dwarf because F#CK YOU, YOUR STAR PLAYER IS NOW DEADER.
The multiplayer is also fun. I've only played one match so far online but it was so fun and competitive that I can see myself going back to it once in a while.
Lastly, the commentators are actually quite fun to hear, as they comment on the races of each team, their characters and such. It sucks that the variety of quotes for each one of those is quite low, but hey, can't have everything.
Do I recommend this game? It depends. If you like board games and have tons of patience, then you'll have lots of fun with the game. If however you don't have much of that, stay away FOREVER. The game is HARSH with new players that don't have any damn idea what this game is all about. It also doesn't have Steam Overlay support, which is stupid.
TL;DR Edition: Fun board game ported into an actual video-game. The learning curve and difficulty spikes are some of the most harsh ones for new players, however once you learn about it you'll have tons of fun with it. And the multiplayer is fun too, still with players on it.

This is one of those games. I wish that had a neutral response for a recommendation. However, as a first  timer of this game. I must say it's really fun, and really challening.
First off, this game is great for the fans who played the table-top version. If your a fan of the
board game, then you'll be a fan of the games. Although not perfect, the game is at least enjoyable for the fan.
However, for the casual gamer who didn't play the table top version and decide to get this game for whatever reason. The learning experirence might be "straight-foward" but in reality it requires trial by error. Meaning, in order to get better at the game you'll have to lose a bunch of times in order to get better. My advice? Play with a friend who owns the game. But don't go straight to the multiplayer, the tutorial is there, but it doesn't come across as "helpful" sure it might sound easy enough, but that is why there is the "in-game manual" in that manual it broaden's the game and really get's in-depth.
The game overall has a bunch of stuff: teams with their unique players and stats. You can customize them, and fight in some very amazing locations. You have two modes a Blitz mode that can tailor your experience, and a classic mode that follows the rules of the table-top.
Lastly the game has a "luck" system. Sure it might not be so direct, or it could not exist at all and is mainly player error. What I am trying to say is. If you "rage quit" it's not the games fault. The game has everything right then and there to help you. And if you have to lose in order to win. Go ahead and lose at least you get the experience to make yourself better. Don't hate the game because it's "un-fair" no it's because you need to fully grasp the game's concept and mechanics.
Overall if you like this sort of game. I recommend it.
