Very good side scrolling adventure-action game (as oppose to action-adventure, like Flashback).  There isn't one dumb logic puzzle, like combining an inflatable duck, a coat hanger, and fishing wire to pick up a key that is easily in reach *caugh* Longest Journey *caugh*.  The majority of the game is spent using your gun-mounted flashlight to investigate the environment for clues, backstory, and key items.  On occassion, when combat actually happens, it's a cinch.
The controls deserve some criticism.
They are wonky at first but quickly become natural.  I recommend turning aim-toggle on, otherwise you're holding right click while aiming, firing, or navigating the inventory.  There is an "invisible cursor" on the screen that dictates what direction you face.  Think of playing "The Swapper" without the blue dot, and try to precisely know when you're turning around.  If the developers put a reticule on the screen it would make this easier to get the hang of.  Another strange control scheme is how to access menu items.  Aim with the right trigger, hold shift, press right, press down, press left or right to highlight the item you want, press space.  Believe it or not that gets easy and robotic.
The plot is excellent - you're an AI-Exoskeleton-WarMachine on a mission to keep your human pilot alive after a crash landing into a derelict AI manufacturing plant.  The plant's downfall is told through diaries and scattered notes which, among other things, give depth to your relentless antagonist.  The moods are handled perfectly.  Dialouge and voice acting is top-notch.  The philosophical and ethical choices you must make actually make even a just-finish-the-game gamer like me want to pause and think about how I feel about the decision.
Lastly, like any adventure game, there's a good walkthrough right on steam for those few "...whatever..." puzzle solutions.
Enjoy!

If you are a fan of realism mixed with fantasy, a blending of cultures, and a killer combination of visuals and soundtracks, this dating simulation is for you! The main character is a college aged heroine who gets forced into the realm of fantasy by someone close to her. Not knowing how to handle her new found powers (and her PTSD) she has to choose a partner to aid her. There are currently 4 completed routes (Shou,Takumi, Shinji, and Tatsuya) and one incomplete route (Hikaru) that one can play through.
PROS:
-Soundtrack (I know I say this a lot, but seriously I cannot stop listening to this soundtrack!)
You can listen to the full soundtrack here:
list=PL_kp86cZLY__mGKC_JEr8UGMCJtYcMSwV
-Very different stories that were well written
-Your character’s progression throughout every story is unique to that story, a refreshing take on a dating simulator.
-Beautiful art
CONS and EXPLANATIONS:
-some people think the soundtrack loops too much, however I think part of that could be influenced by how fast you read. I personally never had an issue with looping, but I do read really fast. I also thought the transitions of the track were well done and almost seamless.
-The story interface and paid DLC. The story start as a free download that acts a demoed introduction of the story. In order to romance characters you have to buy the DLC. I do not mind paying for the content as I really enjoyed playing, but was a little surprised that I had to also pay for the short epilogues or after stories for the characters. I was very confused with the interface at first. You have to choose your character and then press read story and pick the chapter in order to start their route. If you finish the route and unlock the Epilogue then you can click on epilogue- read story and do that. The artwork. The music. And even the story. It is all good in the realm of VN and Otome. Now... Though the prologue leaves a bit to be desired, I like that they made it as something you can see before purchasing the entire game. **Short: This game can stand on its own and proudly call itself a Otome, no matter who made it or where its from. Thats for sure!**
Game overall:
- My only critique is the music, wich becomes boring after some loops.
- CS were good but i would have hoped for more (or i'm used to get more of them in other VN/Otome).
+ Other that that the game is unusually polished
+ i personally enjoyed a more western/realistic artstyle for once
+ and the writing was good (both in grammar AND storytelling, with some minor hickups)
+ the maincharacter is normal, in a GOOD way. She reacts grumpy when someone is rude, shes flustered if its the situation but shes not overly anything. The writing conveyed a fully fleshed character wich you shape with your reaktions one by one. I really enjoyed seeing this instead of one blunt character! (though in one rout the writing really changed the protagonist and i was very unhappy with it.)
The Routes:
havend played all but most of them, i wont say much here since i wrote a full review on their particular side... though let me say one thing, they are usually well written. Some are amazing, some are really good, only one disappointed me but the other ones really made up for it, so dont feel put of by that comment!
Conclusion:
Actually this might be my one favourite western VN/Otome (and i played a lot of those).
I still feel like i prefer japanese / "real" Otomes cause they commonly have a different feel for them and are usually even more polished but i (and you, at least i hope) bear in mind that this is made by a small studio and not with the mindset to bluntly copy those - wich is good because it gets it right, and unique!
I have never encountered a western Otome that has such high standarts and i dont regret buying nearly all routs until now. I like the buissness model too, its really fair and makes me actually support the Team/Game.
This game can stand on its own and i'm glad that i tried it! It gives me hope that there will be more games like this one, where people put the love and work into it, wich these games need!

Let me take you back towards the start of the year, when the Clustertruck alpha was publicly released. I downloaded it, booted it up, and- it ran like♥♥♥♥♥♥ It was only in September I learned it had been running  on intergrated graphics. I booted it up on a proper graphics card, and probably put about ten hours into it. I wouldn't have been surprised if it was non-stop.
What I wanted from Clustertruck was more. The alpha had about twenty levels, I think, and the SUPERTRUCK April Fools joke added a few more. But, I wanted more. More abilities. More maps. They'd perfected the formula, and I wanted more of it.
And God Damn did they deliver.
First off, there's a full 90 levels. Each one has a special twist and they rarely feel the same. There's many more abilities (I can't recall the number) and it just feels BRILLIANT. There's also a level editor, and some interesting levels
The graphics are gorgeous. The bloom, the vibrance, it helps give off the exact vibe the level wants to evoke. Music is fantastic, and I wasn't expecting different tracks. The alpha only had one track, and I would be perfectly fine if the full game had one track. But I vastly prefer the music they have now. Like the graphics, it really does evoke the feel of the level.
Gameplay is arguably the most important factor in Clustertruck. You can have a perfectly good amount of fun for £11, but here's a tip from me- try to speedrun this game. You'll be holding down shift a lot more, leaping and running along the side of things you thought you never could, having moments where you wish somebody was recording you, seeing the pros complete levels in a matter of seconds* and trying to get close to their level and maybe, just someday, surpassing them. That's the gameplay. But what makes the gameplay so, so, SO GREAT is the feel. The camera shakes are wonderful. If you land on a truck far away from your original starting point, you'll shake a bit. You get points for doing all kinds of crazy♥♥♥♥♥♥ and the camera shakes as your total score increases. Plus, you also unlock abilities from the points gained in levels, so it practically encourages you to do crazy♥♥♥♥♥♥ True, you could grind, or get better. That learning curve is fair, let me tell you that.
So, does the game have any downsides?
This is where that * comes in.
*Some people have been hacking 0:00 times in, so that sucks.
TL;DR Game is amazing. Fun, wacky, perfected to such a precise point, and definitely, DEFINITELY worth the money it's asking. If you like music, I can also recommend the soundtrack, but you can listen to it in game, if you don't mind the sound of a right Clustertruck behind you.

If you don't, spend several hundred hours dying horribly in order to make enough money to pay off the debt you incurred buying the gun you're supposed to use, only to discover that since ammunition, upgrade maintenance, and equipment all cost money, you're still in perpetual debt.   There is literally no chance that you can enjoy this game without paying real money, because you will always be in competition with people who have spent money on it.  You can tell, because they are the only ones with guns that actually shoot straight, bullets that actually hurt people, and vehicles of any kind whatsoever.  If you want a better WWII shooter, go play Red Orchestra 2.  Or one of the old Call of Duty games.  Or literally any other WWII shooter with a campaign aspect I can think of that can be run on a modern computer.  I guarantee you will have more fun.

This game was an impulse buy and boy am I glad I took the plunge. Metroid is one of my favorite games from my childhood and games that borrow from that explorational style are more than welcome in this modern age of hand-holding and waypoints. The game is dark and immersive, technologically stylized and contains a fresh take on a classic gaming archetype. You are an AI suit tasked with the protection of your nonresponsive human pilot. This plot device enables the player to neatly fall into the familiar gameplay of Metroid games where you unlock more abilities as you progress. The game is fairly short and relatively easy which are my only two complaints. I would have gladly paid more money for a more fleshed out story and additional challenges. As you progress through the game, areas you complete become locked off so there is no backtracking to find additional secrets with unlocked powers, other than the immediate puzzles involving that specific area. The puzzles are pretty straight forward but I did get stumped a few times. At times the game requires you to think outside the box and experiment with interesting combinations found in your inventory and the enviroment. I am very happy with this purchase and I will be looking forward to any future releases.

The game itself is quite fun and the background lore is nicely crafted.
However, when they talk about it being the "first part of a mind-bending trilogy" that does not imply there's so much content they had to split it up.
As a result, the playtime is around 2-3 hours.
Not only that, but all in all there's 3 distinct parts, with the beginning and end area highly linear(except backtracking), and the middle area being the only really "open" one.
The combat mechanics fall short of expectation, even the designer himself said they will rework it for the second part.
There's also some logical fallacies(only naming a few to avoid spoilers) in the game.
You can kneel down behind cover, but not to enter a small cave.
You get a weapon to utilize to protect yourself, but the upgrade to semi-auto-fire only comes way later.(would semi-auto not mean much more efficient protection to begin with?)
Certain puzzles seem to have pretty obvious solutions, which are not included because the designer wanted the solution to be different.
Also, the game ends on a "to be continued" with a plot twist that I feel almost everybody will expect at that time(or in a similar way).
(so the big "omg"-moment it tries to be kind of does not really work, especially since the reveal adds more to the logical fallacies).
Finally, I am disappointed with the upgrade mechanics. Your suit has an on-board camouflage system that you need to activate quite early to bypass a obstacle. After this, it's reduced to a combat mechanic of "cover".
It has no other use anywhere in the game i found, only for dodging in combat. No more puzzles, obstacles, or alternate solutions(not that there ARE any "alternate solutions") you could use it for.
All in all, it was a fun ride...but some aspects made the ride somewhat bumpy, And, while enjoyable, its exceedingly short with no real replayability(except to get the remaining achievements...but since combat is bland and the puzzle solutions stay identical there's really little other reason to play again).
To sum it up:
Pro:
+ Nice graphical style
+ Good background story+atmosphere
+ Good Voice acting
+ except for backtracking, there's few parts that feel "tacked on" to extend lenght.
Cons:
- combat part is bland, puzzle part feels clumsy for mouse+keyboard(instead of clicking and dragging, you have to aim at something with flashlight selected, then press shift to interact and navigate a popup-menu with wasd)
- no alternate puzzle solutions(even for those where another solution would be obvious)
- no real reason to replay(no alternate paths or story choices)
- very very short(I idled for a while to eat dinner and watch a movie. Pure playtime for me was ~2 hours, on first try...that includes running around figuring out the puzzles and finding items to use...if i was to play again I believe i could finish in 20 minutes or so.)
- several logical inconsistencies, little of which i can mention without spoilers, but somewhat breaking immersion.
- a personal aspect: the movement of the suit. It seems a bit too slow, too unresponsive, lacking options(like kneeling/crawling), and a few more frames(e.g. when reversing run direction) would not have hurt either. It's not bad but any sidescrolling combat suit, for me, has to compete with the look and feel of Samus Arans Varia Suit in Metroid Series(to clarify: I do NOT want a morphball or spinjump, but e.g. a option to "roll into cover" while _running_ forward would be appreciated, rather than walking up to an enemy then kneeling down to go into cover. It's about how fluid things seem and look, how natural the movement is. But as said, thats a personal aspect i just thought i share for others who may feel the same).
All in all, know what you get into. Its short(2-3 hours), you will probably play it once or twice, it will probably be fun but not perfect. Decide for yourself how much that is worth to you.
TL:DR
If I knew before what i know now, i would gladly have waited for the "complete trilogy" to  be out, then fetch that in a bundle.
It is a good game that most people will likely enjoy, but for what is offered, the asking price is too high.
So at the current pricing, with the content delivered, no, i can not recommend this game. Your mileage may vary, and were it significantly cheaper, i would probably recommend it(the game is still not a masterpiece, but good enough to warrant that).

This game surprised me. I saw it on Greenlight and voted "No." I saw it in my Store Queue and clicked "Not Interested." Then I saw Jesse Cox playing it on Youtube, and thought well this actually looks more fun than I thought. The gameplay mechanics are pretty solid, and it feels like it actually brings a bit of strategy and planning to the match 3 formula. The art is wonderful, and the characters are actually some of the most fleshed out female characters I've ever seen in a video game. I like how it's not judgemental of characters who may have had children, and it's also one of the most diverse casts I've seen as well without feeling stereotypical.
If you switch between the male and female protagonist, you'll start to notice that all the male pronouns seem to have been recorded separately from the main dialogue and inserted after the fact, which makes an barely noticeable shift in dialogue recording.
Again, I really loved this game, especially on the harder modes, where you have to use all your planning ahead and gift comboing abilities to their utmost in order to clear levels. All in all, though, my wife was better and probably enjoyed the game more so...

Good news, bad news, time.
Good news: This actually isn't a bad Mahjong game and it's certainly worth playing if you don't just get a free one from either Windows, which comes with a free version until Windows 8 or 10, or one of a multitude of them online.
I liked the clear, clean versions of the tiles, however. To be honest, I play this game more for that reason than anything else, simply because they're so much easier to differentiate and take in at a glance, which is really nice for my next like.
All rounds are timed. You have "x" amount of time to finish a level and as you make a match, you get a portion of time back, making this a fun difficulty factor.
Similarly, each level/girl in the progression means the timer goes down faster, so the difficulty goes up. Each girl has a few levels with the final one being the strip-down version (bar going from top to bottom to reveal the outfit beneath.)
If you're interested in the anime girls aspect, they're pretty enough for digital art and they have various outfits with the final level for each girl being an undressing game (no nudity unless there's a patch out there somewhere - I've not looked.) They end up in swimsuits, lingerie and similar attire with minor changes in facial expressions.
Bad news: The premise of this game is winning the levels to get the models into less clothes like a creepy version of strip mohjong. Not really a totally bad thing if that's your interest. No nudity, again (unless there's a patch.)
The worst part of this game are the very few levels you actually get (or girls, depending on your focus.) It's actually a fun game, but it doesn't take you long to get the hang of it and beat it fairly quickly as there also aren't very many tiles per round/level.
If you get this, do make sure it's no more than a dollar or two. Anything more than that, and you've confirmed yourself desperate and, to be fully honest, getting ripped off.

Only four paths available at this time, and they're different enough that it's hard to give an overall review for the game as a whole. If you buy one path and don't find it all that good, it's worth trying at least one other and see if that's more to your taste. In view of this, the app-like DLC format works pretty well. And if you're going to choose just one path, then I'd recommend Taku as being the best action-wise, and less prone to cliche, though it really benefits from playing at least one other path first. The world building is not very well distributed throughout all paths, so you really should start with Shou, which is the second best path anyway and where you get a lot of the basic exposition and world building. Also, part  of the charm of Taku's path is that it explodes the mould that the other three paths establish, so reading it last makes it shine all the brighter.
Overall, it's not the best VN I've played, but it's enjoyable enough. The MC has a great starter story. IMO, the stories needed more focus on her traumatic experience, her struggle for identity, her powers and the new world she's discovered, and a bit less "notice me, sempai!" waffle. The romance plot is not always well integrated into the main plot, is what I'm saying. The MC is also prone to Damsel syndrome, though there are at least a couple of paths where she has agency and feels like she's holding her own. Overall, the antagonists of each path are developed and interesting, and there are good solid side characters too. The guys are somewhat cliched with their problems, but still relatable and they avoid falling into the extremes of their respective tropes. The story arcs are well written enough that I found the last chapters hard to put down before they were over.
The Shinji path is definitely the weakest for all of the points mentioned above. The Taku path is, IMO, the best; more Buffy the Vampire Slayer, less Twilight. Shou is the second best path for action, agency and intrigue. Tatsuya's path has the pro of a really strong, complex antagonist, plus dragons fighting. Can't go wrong with dragons fighting.
In finale, enjoyable enough, no regrets, and I find myself looking forward to the final path, which should hopefully be out soon.

club and no one except the protagonist is knocking down their door? No one else is interested in business clubs, even to pad their resumes? What do you even do in this club? Where are the other people in this university? Does this girl have friends?? WHAT'S GOING ON, PLEASE STOP RUSHING AND TELL ME MORE. Belay that, says the game cheerfully (as it ushers everyone out the door), we've introduced the guys and the rest of the everyday life stuff is irrelevant and unSEXY! We've got to get the actual plot moving! Let's go meet your mom, shall we?

The prologue feels like it was stripped of all the mundane parts to get to the guys quicker, but such abrupt jumps as from "Hey I got to class!" to "The lunch lady was giving me the evil eye" took away from the immersion. How did I get from starting class to lunch without even a passing mention of what happened in between? For an introduction you learn so little about the protagonist and the guys (except vaguely hinting where they fall on the normal/nice or weird/rude meter), one could start the story at the meeting with her mom and not miss anything of value plotwise.
In conclusion: The art is quite pretty and well done, but I thought the prologue could have been more developed and less rushed. Due to the game's haste to get the guys in, it was difficult to get over the irregularity of the narrative and suspend my disbelief enough to enjoy the plot itself. To be fair, this is only the prologue, so it's possible the rest of the game gets better with more focus on an individual guy per route... but the apparent shallowness of the game I did have access to bothered me, enough to make me reluctant to continue. In any case, that's just my personal opinion, but I cannot recommend this game based on my own experience. I would suggest that once the developers are done with all the routes, that they consider packaging the DLCs into the game so there is a more cohesive experience (offsetting the prologue's flaws), and also get away from the existing microtransaction-y model.

I have had this game for about a month, yet I've played as much as did with TF2 or other games that I have enjoyed and owned for more than 2~4 years.
It's as if I've departed this world to live in Calradia instead.
This game may be close to 6 years old, it may look outdated (which it is), and even though I've missed the sale and bought this game at a full price: the only regret I have is that I've spend so much time playing this game and probably that I'll continue to do so. (Can't do anything else!)
Yes, this game has flaws. AI is rather dumb, exploitable in some cases and screws you over in other. Some quests instructions aren't immediately intuitive. FIghts can get a little repetitive, yet auto-resolve functions is as good as "I forfeit button" (Yes, auto-resolving can be seen as cheating by some, but I'm not saying it should give better results than you playing yourself).
But, those flaws are like a barely faint itch you feel once in a while.
Mount and Blades Warband is a new open world you can live in. Skyrim is good, but Calradia (I dare say) is better. It doesn't have the beautiful scenery of the newer games, but Calradia gives you a different sense of wonderlust. I just can't pin point an aspect that makes this game so immersive and interactive.
You end up liking your hero companions, the fellow nobles of your country, as well as some enemy lords you just happen to develop liking of. Of course you make enemies once in a while and have to run after them until you have them locked up in your dungeon. (Keep your petty ransom, He's rotting in there until the war is over!)
I guess one of the best thing about the game is the difficulty. It constantly challenging. It does get eaiser with time as you build a bigger and better army and you and your companions get stronger. However, defeat is always a possiblity and you learn how to play safe and when to tug tail and run. But you eventually find a way to break down the enemy army; and pick the ground where you know you can make a stand and win.
Calradia is riddled with towns and villages and castles. Yet, I also ended up developing affection for my fief. Dumped troops onto it to keep those filthy Swadians away from my land. (Screw you Harlaus!) Those that raided my village got chased, hunted, defeated, and locked up in my dungeon.
There is so many things in this game that can make you love and hate, both in good sense.
Calradia is an ever changing tempest of wars between factions, you ride the shifting tides, get lost in it and enjoy every moment of it.
I do not think it is too late to buy this game now. It is worth every penny (or nickle for us Canadians) even today I'd say.
P.S. - Get Diplomacy Mod, it adds rather critical functions to the game play and interface. Although vanilla is good, it gets better.

Basically nothing enticing or interesting about this game for PC or actual gaming, unfortunately :(
Everything is time gated and extremely grindy, which would be excusable if it wasn't also mind-numbingly boring:
after a dozen levels or so, your enemies now have 4k hp instead of ~500 hp.... starter weapons have 12 dps and midgame weapons have 16 dps. Endgame super-premium (as in pay hundreds of IRL dollars to roll, enchant and upgrade) weapons do just over 20 dps.... 4k hp mooks. Do you want to play?
Nothing redeeming; virtually no strategy, no key press combinations or mechanical skill involved.
And it has the tried-n-true browser-game style endgame  of "who spends the most thousands of hours and money to get slightly more hp and dps than you" and if thye lose their account they're back at square one. A real game, you can play thousands of hours and crush other players without a physical advantage like endgame "ships" or "gear"  (like in any moba, any shooter... even chess).
Pro's:
- this game is auto-clicker friendly! Though if you're savvy enough to know that, you're playing better games
- not too terrible on mobile/touch platforms since the pickings are slim and the geography is littered with so many detestable "games" in the first place
- PVP exists and -is- a redeeming aspect because it provides a social gaming atmosphere, where you coordinate and focus fire your 15 dps weapons on one enemy (and hope they dont have reinforcements/heals on the way) while chain-cc-ing them. So yes, social aspect exists...... but do you really want to associate and mingle with the deplorables who enjoy these kinds of "games"? ;)

Hello, This is my first game review ever! I've never really felt the need to post about a game before but I just had so much fun with this one :). I've played through each of the stages now and I've got to say I love Spore. From the very begining it tests you and makes you grow and develope the instant you start and the opportunities are endless. I love the begining stages very much. Spore is very fun for the first 4 stages. And the Space stage has so much potential! I say that because I feel the last stage lacks a few perks.
When I played through the Space stage I loved Enhancing the plantes. I love all the cute trees and animals. Its the most creative game I have found ever! From Crystal Lakes to Chocolate Swirls and any colour plants you want the choices really are endless. I find myself getting lost in creating plants and expanding my territory. One Complaint about the towns creative system will be at The Bottom. Basically Why do it 10000 times over again?
The Weapon upgrades that made it possible to expand and conqour very easily are great. I was able to expand quite quickly and few enemies stood in my way. Grox Empire Will Fall... Hopefully. On the other hand, the quests system is good aswell, though very confusing at times. It was sometimes a challenge to tell each quest apart and all the territories. (Late in the game it just looks like one big mess of lines)  Quests helped alot with forming alliances and trading routes. Allies and helper ships are a nice aspect.
Now I get into what I think really needs to be improved. ****TUNE IN SPORE DEVELOPERS****
YOU NEED A CLOUR BLIND CABABILITY. My partner tried to play this game and couldn't see the tiny yellow dot at the bottom of the screen to improve planets. I am hoping you make that dot black or bigger.
The layout with plants and the connecting lines has no pattern or system, sometimes it makes the weirdest connections and gets very confusing with other groups. I hope the developers change the way they appear. With clusters of stars connected with thin lines maybe groups of 5 - 10 closests stars. It would also help with collecting resources and saving time for funner stuff!
The resource collection system is tedious and time consuming, By time I beat the space stage I belive I had 10 Planets and quite a few trading routes. Having to go to each star and hover over each planet to collect its resources was very boring and time consuming, I hope they develope a drone system. Someway to collect the Spice without wasting time. With the system mentioned above maybe They could have cluster markets. A large astroid that is a common marketplace for the cultures. So you dont have to hunt around for the best weapon deals and Spice or Treasure Prices. Somewhere it would show how much everyones willing to bid so you could sell it all at once.
Get rid of the trading route capasity! I hated having to pick and choose who to trade with. Or being rejecting constantly because I have too many. The trading route capasity is 5 or so. It should be depending on your planet number a 1:1 ratio.
I hope the developers one day see this, Because I would Loooove if they added a main trading station. One you can place and hire drones to collect your planet resources. That can hold maybe 100 Spice to start and 10000000 Spice withnall the upgrades.

I know I haven't played this game much, but hear me out. From what I understand, this is a wonderful game. I've not once heard anyone say that Morrowind sucked. However, I caution this:
- The graphics have not aged well, which, I know is a deterent for many (myself included)
- The combat system is frustrating. Unlike Skyrim and Oblivion, Morrowind runs on a dice roll system, which means that even if your weapon makes contact with the enemy, you might still have an awful roll, and you miss anyways. So if you miss, you miss, and if you hit, you still miss half of the time.
I will still rate this game as positive as I have only heard good of this game. So, if you can get past the aforementioned points, I recommend you buy this game. If they sound like an issue, then I recommend saving your money. It may be a great game, but it really doesn't matter if the graphics and mechanics are frustrating.

so since you guys liked my pie recipe im going to give you a butterscotch cinnamon pie recipe.
ITEMS
Butter                    2 oz (½ stick)
Brown Sugar         ½ cup
Water                    2 TBSP
Whole Milk            2 cup
Heavy Cream        1 cup
Brown Sugar         ¼ cup
Egg Yolks              9 ea
Corn Starch           3 TBSP
Cinnamon              2 tsp
Pie Crust (see above)
EQUIP
Small sauce pot
Medium sauce pot
Whisk
Rubber spatula
Measuring cup with a spout for pouring
Large bowl
Candy thermometer (optional)
1) Preheat the oven to 350F
2) Place the 2 oz of butter in the small sauce pot over medium heat. We will be browning the butter here (burre noisette) so you want to keep it on the heat until it stops bubbling but be careful to take it off before it burns. After the bubbles stop you’ll be able to see the specks at the bottom of the pan (milk solids) begin to brown and give off one of the best smells in the world. Remove from the heat and set aside to cool.
3) In another pot combine the milk and heavy cream over medium high heat and cook until the top begins to steam and you can see small bubbles forming along the outside. Remove from the heat and transfer some if not all of the hot liquid to a measuring cup from which you can easily pour it.
4) In a medium sauce pot place the ½ cup of brown sugar (I like dark brown sugar for this recipe, but light brown is fine as well) and the water over medium heat. We’ll be cooking the sugar to ~240F so you can use a candy thermometer if you have one. If you don’t have a thermometer you can tell when the sugar is cooked enough when you see the bubbles slow down in speed and get much larger before they pop. Reduce heat to low.

(still) One of the best otome games I have ever played,
Edit: Now that I have played three of the four routes, I feel like I have standing to write a more credible review. I do have some problems despite it being a game that I would still recommend
HUGE DISCLAIMER: Despite what it says on the page the game is not free. After the prolouge, you need to purchase the routes as "DLCs", rather than making a full purchace. So if you do not like this payment model, do yourself a favour and save yourself from disappointment. This review will also have spoilers so please don't read this if you don't want spoilers.
Coming in, I think I had very low expectations because I find it difficult to find an otome game I am completely satisfied with. I wasn't really a fan of the art style, however after sleuthing around and finding their concept art and Go Fund Me pages, I felt a new appreciation for it. You can tell that a lot of thought and effort went into their character design. The motions are very fluid and the colours used are very beautiful. The stills on their own are even better: I don't really have much to complain about art-wise.
However, I have noticed some of the backdrops they used are recycled and have been used in some other games. I guess I can understand because they are on a budget, but the consistancy was a little off. I felt as if Takumi's route had higher quality, more unique backdrops whereas Tatsuya only had one or two which were unique to his story.
That being said, the story telling is very good. I may have just been biased towards Tatsuya, but I felt his story was a lot better than Takumi's. Shou's was also good, but not as good as Tatsuya's
Here's why: I feel as if the story is far too focused on him and not enough on the main character. We know that she gives up her studies and any relationship she has with her family all to persue her mother, but it never ends up happening. Instead, we only see Takumi's problems: trying to find out how to cure his comatose brother and getting revenge on the people responsible. While it's good that they don't shy away from themes such as substance abuse, I can't help but question the way that they went about it. I was left feeling the character to be weak-willed, when I wanted to empathise with him. Even towards the end, there's no resolution to him "shooting-up" enchancement drugs, let alone mention of it. You see one major relapse in the story, then after the resolution, it's assumed he's suddenly okay. That bothered me. I feel as though they were attempting to make the character edgy, but it fell short because we're not shown anything else substansial to his problem. Is he going to go to a magical rehab? Does his parents know? How would they react? Why isn't Tsubasa doing anything about it? All these things aren't even answered and it's unrealistic to leave these things out. Making Takumi the "rebel" felt like a double-edged sword. They wanted to add more to his character, but they are spreading themselves too thin and have bitten off more than they can chew.
Maybe they go more into detail in his Epilogue and it is more geared towards the main character. If this is the case, that would make it a little better, but I felt a huge lack of closure in Takumi's route in comparision to Tatsuya's or Shou's. I was honestly expecting his to be the best route with how hyped it was, but I ended up liking it the least.
That being said, I was still amazed by how engaged I was by the story, and the originality of the world and characters it portrayed. Even though it's a romance sim, I felt like I was getting so much more than that. The characters felt authentic, raw and no-nonsense. Even though this is fiction, the characters deal with very real problems, and I found it very easy to relate to them.
The opening for the game was absolutely heart-stopping. I loved the ambiance it gave to the entire game and it completely drew me in.
However, I do have a problem with the pricing. While it is worth the money, I didn't like the model they used. It's typical of the Google Play/ IOS platforms you see (Stuff like Voltage Inc.). It's not a big criticism, and I get they probably need as much financial support as possible, but it feels like they are ripping me off. I would have liked the option to pay the game in full, like the other titles on this site, rather than pay $7+ on each character's prologue and epilogue. Again, I understand they are releasing the routes individually, but I would have perferred to wait and have the option to buy the full game.
A lot of content is nice, but it felt too dragged out and long. It would have been nicer if they divided it into more chapters rather than me sitting there for more than 30 minutes just to get though one chapter. Maybe that's just my personal preference.
Overall this is a stellar game for the indie community. It's good enough to compete with giants such as Otomate and Cheritz.
My loyalty is still to Tatsuya, and I highly recommend his story. I Felt Shou's was pretty soild and pleasant to read as well. Takumi's on the other hand is darker and a lot more confronting so if you are okay with drama and angst then it's okay. For me it wasn't really my cup of tea.
I look forward to playing Echos, but I hope they make a second season for these characters. I look forward to reading Hikaru's route when they finally release it. I hope they continue to add and layer this really cool world they created. I find it phenomenal that only 3 people created something this high quality. I would love to pledge, but I don't really have the money for it.
If you're not afraid to spend a little money for a great story, this is definitely something to consider.
(p.s thank you for putting a megane love interest in this game)

Okay, I wanted to wait until I've played through every possibly ending from every route, but, I just couldn't wait because y'all need to know that this game. Is freaking. Amazing. Hands down, the beST visual novel I've ever had the opportunity to experience. 1 MILLION/10 would recommend oh my god.
Phew. With that out of the way, I'll give a more thorough review of the game and what it has to offer.
MUSIC: 9/10; this game has a dynamic, scintillating soundtrack that changes and flows with the mood of the story as it progresses. The songs aren't too busy that they distract you from reading, in fact, they support the words. I found myself easily picturing and creating in my mind the scenes before me. Certain tracks are repeated, but, I don't mind. It did get a tiny bit old after the third route, but, with Takumi's route, there were some pretty sexy saxophone tunes that I really enjoyed. Hopefully with the release of Hikaru's route, there will be new music added as well.
ART: 20/10; what first drew me in from the very beginning browsing the store was the artwork. the art is more realistic, as opposed to the usual manga/anime style drawings you find in other otomes. I found that very refreshing, and I was able to relate to the characters more deeply because of that. The sprites are immaculate, each with countless different expressions, including side characters, that really helped solidify the emotions protrayed in the plot. The backgrounds are polished and vibrant. Everything about this game is so aesthetically pleasing, I'm seriously so amazed by the hard work the developers must have put in to make this game look so good.
PLOT: I loved how each route you took was completely different in regards to pacing and character development, yet, they all occured within the same functioning universe. It always made me curious as to how the other characters solved their particular dilemma without the main character there to help them. For example: what happened to Tatsuya's
Or what about
I'm the type of person who wants to know all the details, so, I'm left wondering.
TATSUYA: talk about tsundere, oh my goodness, my all time weakness. I am proud to say that I got the Mystic Ending on my first try. When I went in search of guides, I saw people were having trouble, but, I guess I love tsunderes too much that I'm an expert at getting them to like me in otomes. I have to say, in terms of character development and substance, Tatsuya's route has to be my favorite. Not just because his character troupe is my kryptonite, but, because it was long enough that I was able to get to know almost every aspect of his life. I teared up a few times, I won't lie. I loved slowly breaking down Tatsuya's walls and seeing the mushy man inside.
SHOU: okay, I usually don't like the ditzy, happy virus types, but, Shou was pretty much the exact opposite of Tatsuya (literally if you look at their powers). I went into his route prepared to be indifferent, but, I actually fell in love with him. He's so pure and honest, he wears his heart on his sleeve, simply precious. I was disappointed that his route was so short compared to the others, especially right after having played through Tatsuya's monster of a route (16 chapters total). I found myself wanting to go deeper and wanting to know more about Shou and the intricacies of his creature community (again, much like we do in Tatsuya's route). But, I took it in stride, and it was still an enjoyable route.
SHINJI: Shinji was a bit of a wild card to me. I didn't really know what kind of character he was going to be, and, going through his route and getting to know him, I still don't quite understand him. He's very closed off, but still very polite. It took forever to get to the real him, pretty much the last chapter
is when the real Shinji appears. I changed MC's name to Miku, which was funny because Shinki's mother's name is Miki, so, there were a few mixups on my part lol.
TAKUMI: talk about a total change of pace, rollercoaster, whirlwind of emotions all at once. Cheese and crackers, Takumi's route felt like I was playing a completely different game than the other three, I'm not even kidding. I could tell without checking that the same person wrote Takumi and Tatsuya's routes, because of writing style, and length, and how they went in depth for every aspect of the plot, including side characters, which I greatly appreciated. Action packed, I was on the edge of my seat the entire time. If I didn't have to go to work, I'd have plowed through the entire route in one sitting. I adore Takumi. He's funny, adorable, and stubborn. A little like Tatsuya in that sense, but more like an overgrown puppy. I found his route to be the saddest, however, in the end, even if it was 'happy'.
HIKARU: Since this is my first review, I'm not sure if I'm able to edit this after I've played Hikaru's route when it's released, but, I'll definitely be back to post my thoughts on that. I seriously cannot wait, I'm waiting with bated breath because I have a feeling his route is going to be epic.
TL;DR I HANDS DOWN RECOMMEND THIS GAME. PURCHASING THE ROUTES IS DEFINITELY WORTH IT. SUPPORT THESE AMAZING DEVELOPERS WHO HAVE CHOSEN TO SHARE THEIR CREATION WITH US.

This is platformer that has non-euclidean rules. In this game falling does not lead to death... unless you land on a trap. The screen wraps left-right and up-down. This is the main mechanic in this platformer. There are numerous puzzles, mostly in the form of determining the path you take to collect all the crystals. Collecting these crystals is the main objective in each level, and you will only be able to proceed once all have been collected. The level ends when the last crystal is obtained, and this is where it becomes rather puzzle-like in route development. There are interesting mechanics that keep the levels fresh, some of which are unique to which "world" you are in. The pixel art and color palette are appealing. The only real complaint would be the hitboxes are slightly larger than one would anticipate on some traps.
This game is $1 USD or whatever your national equivalent might be. If platformers are not your thing or you are easily frustrated, this game might not be for you. The number of levels combined with not encountering any bugs makes this game well worth that dollar. Fun platformer with a pleasant soundtrack.

I never really made a real review. It might be a long review. And yes there is gonna be a TL;DR.
The game started out in 2010 as a new WWII FPS combined with a RTS that influences eachother. After long development, in 2011 people started to get access to the game. It was great for its time, big maps and good graphics. In 2012/2013 is reached Beta, the game went public and you didn't need a gamekey to get access to it. New stuff was added in Builds, starting from A/Z with names of Generals, for example the R build was called Rommel. Now the game is again in the C build, but with war heroes. The build the game is now in is Bauer, named after 'Mad' Jack Churchill. In 2014 is was one of the first games to pass through greenlight and at the very top of the steamcharts for Free To Play games.
The current dev team is a company called Reto-Moto Aps. located in Copenhagen. The company was originally founded by some members of Zyrinx and Lemon in 1997 and created IO Interactive and the Hitman series of video games. In 2008 the company reformed and announced that it will focus on multiplayer based games. The name of the company changed to Reto-Moto.
The devs always look on the forums, reddit, twitch etc. They interact with the community, taking suggestions, using usermade ideas for then game. Etc. Etc. They even run a Weekly developer stream where questions can be asked, new things get shown for the next build, statics shown from the game etc. (I will leave links to the community related pages in a spoiler at the end.) And on twitch, if a streamer is big enough, he can recieve vouchers that you can redeem of ingame premium currency, that can be used for anything.
Now the graphics have been toned down because of people complaining that their potato PCs couldn't handle the game and its 2km²+ maps. There are 3 factions, the US, Germans and Soviets. They all have their own weapons. There are 30+ vehicles and 40+ Weapons available and all accesable WITHOUT any money, it might be a grind. But it gives you a goal.
There are 2 versions of the First Person shooter, Staged mode and War mode. The staged mode is where you start off to learn the game, grind for weapons etc. It will prepare you for the War mode.
The War mode is the gamemode that gets affected by the Real Time Strategy game, and vice versa. If a battle gets created on the RTS. It starts a FPS game, for example an Assault gamemode gets created. You get 2 teams, the defenders and the attackers, if the attackers capture all the objectives. The town on the RTS gets also captured for the faction that won, if the defenders succesfully defend all objectives. Then the town stays theirs.
The RTS is made out of a giant map of Europe with A LOT of towns, factories, airfields etc. 3000+ to be 'exact'. An officer or general can controll ATs (Assault Teams). These teams can be used to attack or defend a town, each AT has a set amount of resources, for example a single simple Guard unit has 54 Infantry spawns.
There are currently (16-2-2016) 9 maps, divided into 3 gamemodes. Encounter, Skirmish and Assault.
There are 6 character paths, Infantry, Tank Crewman, Pilot, Paratrooper, Recon and General. All unlock at a higher rank. You start as Infantry, when you rise in rank you can choose an other carreer path if you want. You can buy more soldiers that can have different carreer paths.
And EVERYTHING is obtainable without spending a single dime.
Yes, it can be a grindy game, yes you can say there is bullsh*t, but I like the game anyway. I am my self a known person in the community, I help the devs on finding bugs and reporting bugs. I am moderator for a lot of big H&G streamers on Twitch, I used to run a Screenshot contest with reward Premium currency. I like the game, and you might also like it if you spend time in it.
Might have a bad status on steam, but if you enjoy WWII games, FPS games or RTS. I would recommend you to Atleast try the game out, see it for your self. Don't listen to the bad reviews. Go and research stuff about the game your self.
Thanks for reading, tell me what you think in the comments.

so since you guys liked my pie recipe im going to give you a butterscotch cinnamon pie recipe.
ITEMS
Butter                    2 oz (½ stick)
Brown Sugar         ½ cup
Water                    2 TBSP
Whole Milk            2 cup
Heavy Cream        1 cup
Brown Sugar         ¼ cup
Egg Yolks              9 ea
Corn Starch           3 TBSP
Cinnamon              2 tsp
Pie Crust (see above)
EQUIP
Small sauce pot
Medium sauce pot
Whisk
Rubber spatula
Measuring cup with a spout for pouring
Large bowl
Candy thermometer (optional)
1) Preheat the oven to 350F
2) Place the 2 oz of butter in the small sauce pot over medium heat. We will be browning the butter here (burre noisette) so you want to keep it on the heat until it stops bubbling but be careful to take it off before it burns. After the bubbles stop you’ll be able to see the specks at the bottom of the pan (milk solids) begin to brown and give off one of the best smells in the world. Remove from the heat and set aside to cool.
3) In another pot combine the milk and heavy cream over medium high heat and cook until the top begins to steam and you can see small bubbles forming along the outside. Remove from the heat and transfer some if not all of the hot liquid to a measuring cup from which you can easily pour it.
4) In a medium sauce pot place the ½ cup of brown sugar (I like dark brown sugar for this recipe, but light brown is fine as well) and the water over medium heat. We’ll be cooking the sugar to ~240F so you can use a candy thermometer if you have one. If you don’t have a thermometer you can tell when the sugar is cooked enough when you see the bubbles slow down in speed and get much larger before they pop. Reduce heat to low.

Old school horror has never looked better. This is the perfectly polished and atmospheric remake of the classic from 1996. The fact that this was originally developed in 2002 is kinda shocking, taking into consideration it looks better than some "modern" games from nowadays - not only for all the enhancements that Capcom incorporated to re-release this in 2015 but also on how beautiful this game always has been.
//pros
- 1080p-enhanced visuals with remastered textures, backgrounds and 5.1 sound.
- This game is absolutely unforgiving, something which was very well established back then and nowadays we're definitely missing: ammunition is priceless, there's a limited amount to scavenge which forces you to utilize each and every shot wisely. A small inventory, which has you juggling items from your inventory to your warehouse constantly. Deadly zombies, which rely mostly on level of threat and design rather than numbers/hordes, and the return of the classic Ink Ribbons to save the game - all this makes you think twice before you cross each door for the first time.
- The return of the iconic protagonists Jill Valentine and Chris Redfield available in different costumes; these include the classic S.T.A.R.S. uniform (1996/2002) and the B.S.A.A. uniform (2009+) which gives a higher modern touch for newcomers to this ol' entry.
- The overall design of the game is magnificent, combined with the fixed-camera angles which makes it a lot more artistic and cinematic.
- What mostly differs this game from the modern RE entries is the requirement of
: there is no one-way route and no in-game alerts/messages to help you out. You need to figure out where to go next (relying on the map is highly necessary) and where to place the keys/items you find. It's easy to get lost on first playthrough.
//cons
- No 4K support.
- Few areas in the game were left with low quality backgrounds.
- Widescreen mode is incorporated, looks better on nowadays screens of course, but it crops the top and bottom while stretching the original image - Capcom could've avoided this.
- Mouse cursor is visible in-game.
- The same funny (not in a good way) voice acting as the original.
//overall

Video review (including score):
Ben 10 was one of my favorite cartoons back when the original series was airing. That original series was recently rebooted in 2016 and this game is a result of that. While I have not watched the reboot, I just had to play this one for nostalgia's sake.
The game offers ten playable aliens, on top of being able to just play as Ben himself. The player is able to seamlessly transition between the different aliens, each having their own unique special attack and ultimate attack. They also each have a different manner of attacking. XLR8, for example, attacks very rapidly, but with less overall damage, whereas the opposite is true with Four Arms, who has slower, more powerful attacks. Some of the aliens even have ranged attacks, such as Grey Matter. Upgrade has a combination of the two, both physical and ranged attacks. The combo stream is even kept up when switching mid-fight, encouraging the player to use this mechanic more often.
 Well it should not exactly come as a surprise that a game based on a cartoon tries to maintain that same cartoony feeling, but Ben 10 did an excellent job in doing so. From the really bad jokes to the overall look of the game, everything about it just made me feel like I was in one big episode of Ben 10. It was actually quite nostalgic.
The combat in this game basically boils down to using one's basic attack until all of the enemies are defeated. The special abilities may look cool, but they are ultimately useless when compared to just how easy it is to defeat an entire group of enemies by just spamming the basic attack. I barely used any special attacks, sticking with either basic attacks or the ultimate attack, the latter of which just wipes all enemies on the screen at once, but had to be slowly charged up before using. Considering the age group this game is targeted at, the shallow combat is not all that surprising. It makes the game much more accessible. In that regard, the developers have done a great job, but not so much for the general gamer.
Ben 10 features six levels, which took me just over two hours to clear. Outside of those levels, there really is not a whole lot to do. One could go back and hunt down all of the sumo card collectibles, but even then, it would probably only add another hour or so. The game really just does not offer a whole lot in the replayability department. Replaying the levels is not at all exciting, considering just how shallow and repetitive the combat can be.
While the game may be rather well polished overall, there were still a few bugs that I ran into during my playthrough, during the last two levels specifically. The first of which was some sort of hover bug while playing XLR8 on the second-to-last level. Whenever I jumped as XLR8 I would defy gravity, floating down at an extremely slow pace, slower than the glide ability that stinkfly has. I actually used this to my advantage to fly over the platforming elements in that level, using my attack to ground pound when I wanted to stop floating. This did not happen with any of the other aliens, but it also did not negatively affect the experience at all, like the next bug did.
A little over halfway through the last level in the game, I ran into a game-breaking bug while playing as XLR8. I do not know how it was triggered, but I suddenly became invulnerable at the cost of not being able to attack any enemies. Enemies still used their attacks on me, but it had no effect, just like my attacks on them. This prevented me from progressing because each area needs to be cleared of enemies before moving on. I had to restart my game to fix this issue, which placed me at the start of the level. The game is short, so this was not as big an issue as it could have been, but it is still a bug that really needs to be addressed.
Additionally, during the last level, before I ran into that game-breaking bug, I had some sort of issue with my fps. It would slowly deteriorate from the 60 fps it should have been running at down towards 15fps. This was right before I ran into the invulnerability bug, so these two issues may be linked, as both were fixed with a simple restart of the game.
For a game based on a cartoon, Ben 10 does its job. It may have shallow combat, but that makes it very accessible for the audience it is aimed at and that audience will probably enjoy it a lot more than the average gamer. Even so, bugs and a general lack of content negatively affect both parties. I would only recommend this game if you are a fan of the show.

This review comes from someone who used to love the show as a kid, and still holds a bit of nostalgia. I've also played almost every major Ben 10 game (excluding omniverse 2) - all of which i thought were on the poor side provided the potential. Yes, i'm aware this game is made directly for kids, despite that being the case its a really weak game. Ben 10 has also been around for almost 12 years now, and has bizarrely gotten more childish over the past few years.
Can someone PLEASE make a large scale Ben 10 RPG? Every single Ben 10 game has been made to milk money from the merchandise, rather than to attract the gaming audience and make the show bigger in the process. There's a lot that's possible with the huge number of aliens that were in the previous Ben 10 series. So much potential with this IP that's going unrealized.
Add in around 30+ aliens with their own set of unique moves. More aliens could be added over time with updates. Not every player has to be Ben either, you can create your own character and the story/premise could be something along the lines of:
'The Omnitrix has been made available for human kind. Factions and Omnitrix variants are available for anyone to choose from, each yielding their own advantages and disadvantages. Factions are at war with one another, and several species wage war against humans for the power of the Omnitrix. Fight your battle and uncover the secrets behind this new order.'
Make it difficult and rewarding to unlock certain aliens, similar to unlocking Pokemon. Doesn't have to be a linear single player game either, it could be a large open world with many hidden bosses and a multiplayer mode. Battling other players with your unlocked aliens, changing aliens during a battle to best the other player would be amazing. Add a ton of variation to the world too. Good graphics would also be welcome, we're in 2017 now. Get some inspiration from PlatinumGames on how to do good combat. Even Black Desert Online is a good game to refer to and learn from. Yes, i'm aware making combat fun and challenging is a highly difficult task for anyone (as well as designing lots of playable aliens). It's far from impossible though, and it takes effort and work to make a game good. The ability to change into different aliens with great abilities should be a magnificent thing to be able to do. Make each alien understood, with the right moveset that compliments each and every one. You can also make Vilgax a super hard boss fight that almost no one can complete due to the immense, yet structured difficulty. Beating him would allow you to unlock one ultimate version for any of your aliens, or something. Still needs a good rewarding system after all, perhaps a few veteran level bosses that allow you to unlock ultimates or extra moves? Of course, maybe a special super secret boss where you can fight Ben 10 himself. You should even be able to surf through different places, like the null void where you can fight endless swarms of massive creatures, perhaps using a wave mode and leaderboards. You can even team up with other players for team based battles. I'm aware its dangerous to dream for this, but hope the right people hear my voice.
Referring now to this newly released game, each alien deserves the right treatment. Not just some quick ultimate move that literally does the same job for all aliens. Absolutely no effort was put into this Ben 10 game. The only plus i can give this is that they finally added some of the original 10 in a video-game (sort of). This is still a slightly different 10 aliens compared to the 10 from the original series. However, its made pointless playing as more than one alien regardless, when almost everyone is the same. All you do is hit, counter, hit hit, counter and special. Then you unlock your ultimate move every once in a while which is also boring after the first couple of times per alien. There's no gameplay narrative present either, you just progress through the areas and fight enemies. No puzzles or anything else. The only thing available besides combat is that you require certain aliens to get to certain places, and all it takes to do that is changing aliens and pressing the required button. It's fine if you want to stick to just combat in a game like this, but not when its the same repeated groups of enemies and the combat is, once again repetitive.
This game is only 2.5gb in size, and that makes sense because of the lack of variation almost anywhere you look, including level design. I've played the first four levels, but got way too bored to complete the game. Every alien repeats their own attack move. No mixing up light and hard attacks for unique combos. What I played so far its a really interesting game. I would consider it a puzzle platformer. You die after one hit, the clue is,  only hazards and enemies kill you. Jumping down a cliff or out of the windows results in the classic labyrinth experience as every border is connected to the level you are playing in. This means that if you go over the border at the right side you appear left, this works with falling, jumping and enemies.
It has a simple story about creation of life, you were made on the sixth day and got the task to collect all the colored crystals to return color to the world. Progress is achieved through buying the next level with your crystals, as you need every crystal to complete a level its a totally fair system. You just have to figure out how to get every crystal without dying as dying resets the level and what you gathered in it.
The music is something experimental, slightly reminding me of Corpse Part during a few parts. There is an option to turn the music off, if you dont like it. Upon death you hear a specific phrase that matches the story.

This is an interesting game in regards of reommendation. The reason why the recommendation is negative is mainly because objectively "bad" and "buggy", on launch there was an issue where the exe was linked improperly, but such issue has been patched out nicely fast too, to be honest. With little polishing, I would imagine that I would very gladly change the "not recommended" tag, if I feel that the game gets polished slightly around the corners.
As for the game itself, I find the game good in design, but bad in the quality of execution. The latter I will cover first:
As said, runing the game may be rather finnique, but not impossible, and the game is riddeled with bugs: The player character does not have an idle sprite facing left, the options are not options but a help screen (as in you can't change anything), the music does not stay off when it's turned off, but rather stops or starts by toggling the music on and off (because of wich I also noticed that screenshots from the game are not fullscreen, but cropped to top left corner). Also the jump is bound to W, Arrow up and Space, but as there are three keys for jusmping (no options = no rebinding), the space is the only key that works on these "Jump boosters". This is partially even game breaking, as every once and a while these boosters are set up as a form of obstacle, but can be circumvented by jumping normally by NOT using space as a jump key. And to add insult to injury, the moving platforms (that are of plenty) do not move (except downwards) while you're on them.
That all said, the hitboxes are consistent, the screenwarping is surprisingly fresh mechanic (in terms of game design) for something that has been around since joust at last, and while the movement does not have any momentum, the controls are tight enough. Added that with nicely casual puzzle levels, and simple mechanics that don't need a tutorial, the game is surprisingly good in design. It feels as if it was made in Games Factory (The predecessor of Multimedia Fusion), but with more care that most put in their god awful unity games.
[EDIT]: Few oversights I forgot to mention; While the levels are properly designed, sometimes there is a situation where an enemy is positioned next to the level start so that it kills the unexpecting player rather surprisingly, and the shooting patterns that there are seem to be random which, in terms of game design, makes playing te game unneccessarily inconsistent, and adds random deaths especially as the shooting entities does not have any tell of when they're shooting.
[EDIT2]: Updated a bug that was fixed, but left description of it for "archival reasons". +1 for developer for acting fast on fixing issues on that.
TL;DR: If you're reading this because you want easy and simple working game, you shouldn't get the game, but if you know what you're getting in to, go ahead.

Well, it's short. I got stumped a few times and still finished the game in just under four hours. It's heavily story-based so the re-play value is probably a bit low -- but that is a problem with the genre, not the game itself.
But was it worth the 10 bucks? Definitely. The art is pretty (if a bit hard to see at times), the sound and voice acting is great and the gameplay is pretty solid. But most importantly: despite the difficulty of some of the puzzles, I enjoyed the game through and through.
Some players were annoyed that the ending is a bit of a cliff-hanger -- but I'd argue that it reveals just enough to allow the game to stand on its own. There are tons of open questions left and it's not guaranteed that they will be answered in any of the future chapters. It's not a game for those who obsess over getting "100%" of a game, but that is intentional. Good storytelling is based on telling you just enough to keep you interested, not boring you with exhaustive details.
A++ would buy again.

I followed the production of this game for a very long time before I finally had the chance to sit down and play it. I was very excited to get the chance to experience something new and to support an indie VN developer. However, I am genuinely sorry to say that I have never before have I been so absolutely and utterly disappointed with a game. I wanted to like it so badly. It looked so promising, so interesting and it fell completely short. If it wasn’t already too late, I would request a refund. Since that isn’t an option, I’ll try and provide as thorough of a review as I possibly can.
ART
The art is lovely, as long as you only look at the sprites. While I saw some inconsistencies with the sprites, overall I would say they are of amazing quality. The sprites are by far the strongest aspect of this game. But only the sprites. The backgrounds were obviously stock and clashed horribly with the art style of the sprites. At times the sprites looked fuzzy and out of place because of the backgrounds, considerably diminishing the immersion.
MUSIC
I see so many people complimenting the OST that I have to wonder if they were actually listening to the same music I was. The tracks are bland and uninteresting and obvious stock material. The tracks do not loop very well, making it painfully obvious when a track suddenly repeats. For the most part, the tracks did fit in well, except for a few that felt incredibly strange and out of style compared to the rest of the OST. You could play this game muted and it would make no difference.
WRITING
The writing was by far the weakest point of the game. The Protagonist is vapid, confusing, and inconsistent. The game provides choices that would suggest you’re about to get some world building, and then immediately back pedals and undermines the player’s curiosity and desire to know more about the world by saying “ask me later” and never bringing it up again. A
character is introduced as a stranger in the game’s prologue, and once you purchase a route you are supposed to believe that he is the Protag’s long lost friend, and then he is never mentioned again. Every unique thing about the protag that is established in the prologue is strangely forgotten until it’s suddenly convenient to bring it up again. Each character route is advertised as its own complete story, but at the end (of at least Shinji’s route) you know absolutely nothing about the protag. You never find out more about her powers, there is hardly any mention of what happened to her mother or the impact on her family or future, she never focuses on her magic beyond plot device, she never deals with her curse, and she has no resolution to her own dilemma. As the game progressed, she became increasingly annoying. Her character development is somewhere between nonexistent and shoddy at best.
Every single time skip felt awkward and unnatural. At times, the game introduces concepts you are simply supposed to accept without questioning. What is this gear thing that instantly changes your clothes like some magical girl anime? Why does the Protag not react to suddenly losing her glasses whenever she transforms? Who knows. I sure don’t.
In Shinji’s route specifically, I was completely disgusted how their fight was handled. They did not talk. They did not apologize to one another. They did not address their issues. Instead, everything was resolved with sex. And that was it. The subject was never brought up again. Because sex resolves everything and fixes all relationship problems. Who needs communication? I’m very glad this is the lesson I walked away with. While I enjoyed Shinji as a character far more than the Protag, he had his own fair share of problems, beyond the whole sex solves everything dilemma. It is stressed multiple times that he is a kind a helpful person, but no examples are ever given to prove this. His big secret with the death magic and ghost possession business feels completely irrelevant. Even when it does come into play, it feels disorganized, like a first time writer trying to make their first OC as cool as possible.
I found multiple typos while reading and dialogue presented underneath the wrong name. I’m pretty certain that Shinji did not intend to call his own father “my darling husband.” On top of that, the GUI is bland and uninteresting.
In the end, I was left starving for more than what I got. I hate the Protagonist, I hate the lack of explanation for anything, I hate how absolutely needless half of the scenes that could have expanded on lore and side characters (who I adored, they were far more interesting than most of the main characters) felt. There was so much potential in this game, and I feel like all of it was wasted. Since I bought this game with Christmas money from my twin and I wish to honor his gift in every way, I'll continue to play what I purchased. Maybe my opinion will change, and I desperately hope that it does. If so, I'll gladly update this review.
But as of right now, honestly, in my eyes the only thing that made this game even remotely worth my poor brother's money was Shinji ripping out a still beating heart. That was beautiful.
TL;DR
Play something else. There are other indie developers more deserving of your time and money.

Some updates have been released for this game that call for an update on my old review! My last review was back on August 31st, and new features have been implemented that make the game more accessible and enjoyable.
Let me start my review by cutting straight to the chase:
This game is not meant for H-Fans. It is meant for mahjong fans that appreciate fanservice. If you aren't a big fan of mahjong, then it doesn't matter how much you like cute girls, you're not going to enjoy this game.
There is no actual nudity. If you're looking for explicit nudity then you'll have to go somewhere else.
Tl,dr version: You play mahjong. A LOT of mahjong. And in doing so you unlock new outfits for the girls that you can ogle them in.
With that out of the way...
Pretty Girls Mahjong Solitaire is exactly as described. You play mahjong to strip cute girls! The game has five different girls, and each girl has several stages; each stage consists of 1 new outfit to unlock and 3 different Mahjong Solitaire puzzles to beat to reveal that outfit. You play the stages in order; the first stage will usually just consist of some kind of job attire, while the remaining stages will grant you increasingly suggestive outfits.
While there are five different girls, you start with only one of them immediately available--Rin. To unlock the other four girls, you must complete the stages and unlock the outfits of the girls already available.
The five girls and their number of stages/extra outfits are as follows:
Rin: 4 Stages
Risa: 3 Stages
Kanon: 3 Stages
Erina: 3 Stages
Ayame: 4 Stages
After beating a stage and unveiling the given stage's outfit, you can return to the main menu to select the "Dressing Room" feature, which lets you doll up the girls you've unlocked in any of the given girl's outfits that you've revealed. Before the 8/30/2016 patch, the Dressing Room would only display the outfits full-body, without a zoom feature. Afterwards, the game was given a Zoom feature, supposedly so that you can ogle the girls at higher resolution... buuut, it didn't work.
This has since been sort-of fixed. The Dressing Room now displays the girls at a higher resolution by default; there's still no zoom-in or zoom-out option, but as a personal preference I enjoy having a higher resolution to look at.
On to the actual Mahjong game itself, though. By default, it plays just like classic mahjong. You're on a timer that slowly ticks down as you play; as you match tiles on the board, they'll fill up the timer slightly to give you a longer time to think. Simple enough. However, unlike most Mahjong games, it did not come with a Hint or Shuffle option, meaning that if you ran into the bogus situation of two tiles being unfairly stacked atop one another, then that was it. Game over, time to restart the round.
HOWEVER, this has since been remedied with an "easy mode". Easy mode is accessible through the options menu in the main menu; this option adds "Suggested Move" and "Shuffle" actions on every puzzle, as well as taking away the timer so you don't have to rush. It makes the game a lot more relaxed and does not take away the rewards from completing stages--you'll still get the outfit unlocked for the dressing room if you clear the given puzzle, and you'll still unlock steam Achievements. There's literally no reason not to use Easy mode unless you just really want a frustrating challenge.
In summary...
I find this game to be fun because I'm something of a fan of Mahjong Solitaire in the first place. Easy mode makes the game much more accessible to newcomers than it used to be, and makes the game much less stressful to play than it'd been prior to the update.
The suggestive outfits on the girls are nice and fun to look at, and the fact you can then check them out at any time in the dressing room is a nice feature to have. It does feel like more could have been done with the game's available features; for starters, it would be nice to have a sort of Free-Play mode where you can just continually have puzzles thrown at you at random. Also, the dressing room, while a very nice feature, feels somewhat lacking.
I also feel that there should be a sort of "In-between" difficulty that isn't quite Easy but isn't quite "normal"(as the game puts it); truth be told I was somewhat thrown off guard by the fact that the timer was completely removed for Easy Mode. I think a "Normal Mode" in which the Hint and Shuffle options are still available but the timer still exists would be a good implementation.
In the end, I give Pretty Girls Mahjong Solitaire two separate scores: One for Mahjong fans, and one for people who aren't fans of mahjong (newcomers to the game):
For Fans: I give this game a
For Non-fans: I give this game a
I still don't believe that the game is quite worth full-price at $15, but it's much better than it was, and if you have an extra fifteen bucks laying around burning a hole in your pocket, I say "why not?". It may be worthwhile to wait until the game is on sale for $10 or less, however.
